title: Comment On "Scalable Quantum Machine Learning: Trainability, Expressivity And Efficiency": Polynomial Evaluation Of The Triplet-Block Readout
authors: Erfan Amidi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the classical-cost claim for the triplet-block two-body readout in arXiv:2607.24014v1. The Gaussian-state expansion used there gives an [MATH] classical algorithm, but it is not necessary for fixed-body observables. The triplet-block input has an explicitly computable diagonal two-particle reduced density matrix, which passive fermionic linear optics propagates through [MATH]. This gives a deterministic [MATH] algorithm for the complete correlator vector [MATH], independently of [MATH] and the fermionic-linear-optics extent. More generally, every number-conserving fixed-[MATH]-body expectation is polynomially computable whenever the input [MATH]-particle reduced density matrix is classically available; if that matrix is diagonal, all diagonal correlators are computable in [MATH] time. This invalidates the algorithm-relative exponential-cost conclusion for the supervised two-body readout, without affecting the gradient-variance, barren-plateau, parameter-shift, or sampling-hardness results.
tldr: This comment provides a polynomial-time classical algorithm for evaluating the triplet-block readout in the discussed quantum machine learning scheme, contradicting the original paper's exponential-cost claim.
motivation: The original paper claimed an exponential classical cost for the two-body readout; this comment shows that a simpler classical computation suffices using explicit reduced density matrices.
method: By using the diagonal two-particle reduced density matrix and passive fermionic linear optics, the author derives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the correlator vector, independent of system size and extent.
result: The polynomial algorithm invalidates the exponential-cost conclusion for the readout, though other results such as gradient variance and sampling hardness remain unaffected.
conclusion: The comment corrects the complexity assessment of the supervised two-body readout, highlighting the importance of considering fixed-body observables.

title: Granthi: Higher-Order Quantum Programming Via Unitary Wiring
authors: Radha Jagadeesan Samson Abramsky
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing quantum programming languages confine higher order structure to a classical host while restricting the quantum layer to first order operations on qubits. This paper presents Granthi, a purely unitary higher-order quantum programming language built on three design commitments: quantum programs are first class values that may be passed, returned, and coherently composed; additive structure is tag-preserving routing rather than observational branching, so control may remain in superposition; and programmer-facing finite label types with named reversible operations provide domain-level control spaces without exposing tag management. Every well-typed term, including at function type, denotes a unitary on its boundary interface, and the compiler realizes exactly its wiring as a quantum circuit on the physical qubit layout (assuming correctness of the pytket backend). Granthi is implemented end-to-end: an OCaml DSL elaborates surface programs through a binder-free core IR to executable quantum circuits via pytket. The language directly supports the quantum switch, compiled to a static circuit, as well as interference on control-flow history and structured finite control, all within the purely unitary fragment.
tldr: Presents Granthi, a purely unitary higher-order quantum programming language that ensures all well-typed terms denote unitaries, enabling coherent composition and control.
motivation: Existing quantum programming languages restrict higher-order structure to a classical host, limiting expressiveness and the ability to keep control in superposition.
method: Designs a language with tag-preserving routing, named reversible operations, and a compiler from an OCaml DSL to quantum circuits via pytket.
result: Every well-typed term, including function types, admits a unitary boundary, and the compiler realizes the exact wiring as a quantum circuit, supporting features like the quantum switch.
conclusion: Provides an end-to-end implementation of a purely unitary higher-order quantum programming language, advancing quantum programming language design.

title: Scaling Behavior Of Parameterized Quantum Circuits From A Lie-Algebraic Perspective
authors: Hiroshi Ohno
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how the performance of parameterized quantum circuits scales with available resources is important for characterizing their trainability and effective model capacity. In this study, we numerically investigate data scaling, model scaling, and compute scaling in parameterized quantum circuits and examine Lie-algebraic quantities as alternative measures of model size. In addition to the number of circuit parameters, we consider the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra, the observable-orbit dimension, and a Jacobian effective dimension defined as the rank of the Jacobian of the parameterized observable orbit. Using a regression task with randomly generated Pauli-string generators, we observe decreasing loss with increasing training dataset size, parameter size, and number of optimization iterations over the ranges investigated. For model scaling, the dynamical Lie algebra and observable orbit dimensions rapidly saturate as the parameter size increases, whereas the Jacobian effective dimension remains strongly correlated with the parameter size and exhibits comparable scaling behavior. These results suggest that the Jacobian effective dimension provides a geometry-aware measure of the locally accessible observable degrees of freedom of finite-depth parameterized quantum circuits and may serve as a useful scaling parameter beyond the nominal parameter size.
tldr: This paper numerically investigates the scaling behavior of parameterized quantum circuits using Lie-algebraic measures, finding that the Jacobian effective dimension correlates with parameter size better than other measures.
motivation: Understanding how performance scales with resources is important for characterizing trainability and effective model capacity of parameterized quantum circuits.
method: The author performs numerical experiments with randomly generated Pauli-string generators, comparing data scaling, model scaling, and compute scaling, and evaluates the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra, observable-orbit dimension, and Jacobian effective dimension as alternative model size measures.
result: Loss decreases with increasing dataset size, parameter size, and optimization iterations; the dynamical Lie algebra and observable-orbit dimensions saturate quickly, while the Jacobian effective dimension remains strongly correlated with parameter size and exhibits comparable scaling behavior.
conclusion: The Jacobian effective dimension provides a geometry-aware measure of locally accessible observable degrees of freedom and may serve as a useful scaling parameter beyond nominal parameter size.

title: Predicting Resource Efficient Hamiltonian Decomposition For Continuous-Time Quantum Walk Simulations
authors: Mostafa Atallah, Rebekah Herrman, Zain H. Saleem
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) on a graph in the circuit model of quantum computing requires decomposing its Hamiltonian into terms that can be Trotterized into hardware-native gates. We consider two such decompositions: the standard Pauli decomposition and the recently introduced matching decomposition. Prior work suggests that the matching decomposition uses fewer CX gates on sparse graphs, while the Pauli decomposition uses fewer on denser graphs. Since CX gates dominate error and runtime on current hardware, we train machine learning models to predict, for a given graph, which of the two decompositions produces the smaller CX gate count. We train and evaluate on the complete population of all 11,117 connected eight-vertex graphs from Brendan McKay's database, so the class balance and overlap are measured directly rather than estimated. We use twelve features: ten topological properties of the graph and two that count the terms the Pauli and matching decompositions produce (n_Pauli and n_match), both computable without transpiling the simulation circuit. Standard topological properties alone provide little predictive power. Instead, the dominant signal comes from n_Pauli, a property of the Hamiltonian decomposition rather than an intrinsic property of the graph; degree variance is the only other feature that carries signal. Across a range of models the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) falls in a narrow band, from 0.569 untuned to 0.593 after tuning, so no single architecture stands out. We adopt a single-hidden-layer neural network at MCC 0.593. Applied frozen to a held-out, class-balanced test set of larger graphs (up to 256 vertices) from structured and Erdos-Renyi families, the model transfers, with MCC rising from 0.785 at N=8 to 1 at N>=64.
tldr: The paper trains machine learning models to predict whether Pauli or matching Hamiltonian decomposition uses fewer CX gates for continuous-time quantum walk simulations, achieving transferable predictions across graph sizes.
motivation: CX gates dominate error and runtime in quantum circuits, so choosing a decomposition that minimizes CX count can improve simulation efficiency.
method: Twelve features (ten topological graph properties plus the decomposition term counts n_Pauli and n_match) are used to train various ML models, with a single-hidden-layer neural network adopted after tuning.
result: Topological features have little predictive power; the dominant signal is n_Pauli. The final model reaches MCC 0.593 on 8-vertex graphs and transfers to larger graphs (MCC up to 1 for N≥64).
conclusion: The decomposition term count, especially n_Pauli, is the key predictor for choosing the more resource-efficient decomposition, enabling practical optimization of quantum walk simulations.

title: Differentiable High-fidelity Vectorial Propagator
authors: Jonghwa Shin Dohyun Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The numerical accuracy and computational efficiency of free-space field propagation directly determine what physics can be predicted and what devices can be designed, from nanophotonic metasurfaces to optically addressed quantum processors. Existing methods face a fundamental accuracy-speed trade-off, which is further compounded in the vectorial regime, where major formalisms remain fragmented with no unified computational framework. Here we address both challenges: a theory that unifies the vectorial diffraction framework, and an algorithm that resolves the accuracy-speed trade-off, each reinforcing the other. We prove that all major vectorial diffraction formalisms and vector-potential seeding methods arise from a single surface equivalence principle and reduce, without approximation, to a finite sequence of scalar angular-spectrum operations. Any advance in scalar propagation can therefore be exploited across the entire vectorial ecosystem. The error-compensating angular spectrum method (E-ASM) serves as a fast and accurate scalar solver, delivering peak signal-to-noise-ratio gains exceeding 60 dB over the state-of-the-art band-extended angular spectrum method at order-of-magnitude faster speed, with a freely configurable observation window. Their combination, implemented in a GPU-accelerated, fully differentiable form, turns rigorous vectorial field computation, previously prohibitive for higher-order beams over macroscopic distances, into a practical, inverse-design-ready tool. We demonstrate the framework on optically addressed local qubit gates and on vectorial Hermite-Gaussian and Laguerre-Gaussian beam propagation, resolving field structures inaccessible to scalar or approximate vectorial methods.
tldr: This paper presents a unified vectorial diffraction framework and a fast, accurate, differentiable propagation algorithm for free-space fields, demonstrated on optically addressed qubit gates and beam propagation.
motivation: Existing methods for free-space field propagation suffer from accuracy-speed trade-offs, especially in vectorial regimes, with fragmented formalisms. The authors aim to unify these formalisms and provide a computationally efficient solver.
method: They prove that all major vectorial diffraction formalisms reduce to scalar angular-spectrum operations via surface equivalence, then use an error-compensating angular spectrum method (E-ASM) as a fast scalar solver, implemented in a GPU-accelerated differentiable form.
result: The framework achieves over 60 dB PSNR improvement over state-of-the-art methods with order-of-magnitude speedup, and enables computation of vectorial fields for higher-order beams and optically addressed qubit gates.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for high-fidelity vectorial field computation, making it feasible for inverse design in optical quantum systems.

title: Non-Hermitian Sensing Via End-to-end Green's Functions
authors: Hui-Qiang Liang, Yu-Shi Cheng, Guo-Fu Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensing hinges on two key attributes: high sensitivity and resilience to noise. Here, we present a scheme that unites these features within a single framework. By harnessing the exponential amplification of end-to-end Green's functions-a direct signature of the non-Hermitian skin effect-our scheme achieves an exponential sensitivity scaling of exp({\alpha}L) with {\alpha} a model-specific constant and L the system size. Notably, this enhanced sensitivity is protected by spectral winding numbers and endures under disorder when the non-Hermitian topological phase remains intact. We also explore its feasibility in synthetic non-Hermitian platforms, providing a pathway toward highly sensitive and noise-tolerant sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a sensing scheme that exploits the non-Hermitian skin effect to achieve exponential sensitivity scaling with system size, while maintaining robustness to disorder.
motivation: Sensing requires both high sensitivity and resilience to noise, which are often challenging to combine. The authors aim to unify these features using non-Hermitian physics.
method: The scheme leverages end-to-end Green's functions in non-Hermitian systems, where exponential amplification arises from the skin effect. Sensitivity is protected by spectral winding numbers and remains intact under disorder when the non-Hermitian topological phase persists.
result: The approach achieves an exponential sensitivity scaling of exp(αL) with α a model-specific constant and L the system size, and demonstrates robustness in synthetic non-Hermitian platforms.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway toward highly sensitive and noise-tolerant sensing, leveraging topological protection in non-Hermitian systems.

title: Resolving Positive Semi-definiteness In Physics-informed Kernels For Scientific Machine Learning
authors: J. Moser, C. Albert, S. Ranftl
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many modern machine learning models can be understood as kernel-based function-space models, including Gaussian processes and neural tangent kernels. In scientific machine learning, differential operators are increasingly used to encode physical structure directly into such models. However, it has remained unclear under which conditions these constructions are valid machine learning models, i.e. preserve positive semi-definiteness, and whether observed instabilities arise from ill-posed modeling or numerical effects. Here, we establish a simple and sufficient condition for positive semi-definiteness: for linear differential operators of order m, the base kernel must be m-times continuously differentiable. Crucially, this guarantee holds for operators with non-constant and even discontinuous coefficients. Examples are ubiquitous in physical systems, including diffusion, material elasticity, wave propagation in inhomogeneous media, and quantum systems. We conclude that remaining instabilities are attributable to numerical issues, providing a unifying validity foundation for operator-informed kernel methods.
tldr: The paper establishes a sufficient condition for positive semi-definiteness in physics-informed kernel methods using differential operators, with applications to various physical systems.
motivation: To clarify when differential operators can be integrated into kernel-based models without compromising model validity, since instabilities may arise from ill-posed modeling or numerical issues.
method: They derive a simple condition: for linear differential operators of order m, the base kernel must be m-times continuously differentiable, which works even for non-constant or discontinuous coefficients.
result: They prove this condition mathematically, showing that remaining instabilities are numerical rather than modeling issues, thus providing a unifying validity foundation.
conclusion: This work ensures that operator-informed kernel methods are valid across many physical systems, including quantum, diffusion, and elasticity, by guaranteeing positive semi-definiteness.

title: On The Drinfeld Center Of The Verlinde Category $\Ver_p$
authors: Victor Ostrik Shlomo Gelaki
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide some information about the Drinfeld center [MATH] of the Verlinde category [MATH]. We compute explicitly the Cartan matrix, bound quiver and cohomology of [MATH], and prove that the category [MATH] is wild for every [MATH]. In the special case [MATH], we show that [MATH] has exactly [MATH] non-isomorphic indecomposable objects, classify them and describe the Green ring of [MATH], and compute the semisimplification of [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies the Drinfeld center of the Verlinde category, computing its Cartan matrix, bound quiver, cohomology, and proving that it is wild for all p, with a detailed classification for a special case.
motivation: To understand the structure of the Drinfeld center of a key example of a modular tensor category, which is important in pure mathematics and potentially in topological quantum computation.
method: Uses categorical and representation-theoretic techniques to compute explicit invariants and analyze the representation type.
result: Computes the Cartan matrix, bound quiver, and cohomology, proves wildness for all p, and for a special case classifies all indecomposable objects and describes the Green ring.
conclusion: The Drinfeld center is wild in general, indicating complex representation theory, but the special case has a finite number of indecomposables, providing a manageable subcategory.

title: Revealing Physical Redundancy In The Two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard Model Via Transferable Observable Reconstruction
authors: Ao-Ning Wang, Min-Quan He, Z. D. Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Fermi-Hubbard model provides a paradigmatic setting for studying strongly correlated quantum matter, where different observables are commonly used to probe charge, interaction, and spin correlations. In this work, we investigate whether these observables contain mutually transferable physical information beyond their apparent distinction. We quantify such physical redundancy through transferability tests among three representative observables of the two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model: total density (N), double occupancy (D), and spin-spin correlation (S). Using a neural-network reconstruction framework, we find that the phase diagram of one observable can be reconstructed from another with accuracy close to self-reconstruction benchmarks, especially in trivial phase regimes. This transferability relies on correct physical labeling, persists across finite-temperature regimes, and remains robust under noisy inputs. Our results suggest that separate observables can carry a substantial fraction of one another's physical information, providing numerical evidence for observable-level redundancy in the two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard system.
tldr: The paper demonstrates through neural-network reconstruction that distinct observables in the 2D Fermi-Hubbard model carry mutually transferable physical information, indicating observable-level redundancy.
motivation: To investigate whether different physical observables in strongly correlated quantum systems contain mutually transferable information beyond their apparent distinction, and to quantify this redundancy.
method: A neural-network reconstruction framework is used to test transferability among three observables (total density, double occupancy, spin-spin correlation) across phase regimes and temperatures, including noisy inputs.
result: The phase diagram of one observable can be reconstructed from another with accuracy close to self-reconstruction, especially in trivial phases, and this transferability persists across temperatures and under noise.
conclusion: The results provide numerical evidence for observable-level redundancy in the Fermi-Hubbard model, suggesting that separate observables carry a substantial fraction of each other's physical information.

title: Morphological Representation Theory In The Fourier Inf-Semilattice: Universal Decomposition Of Frequency-Domain Deep Learning Operators
authors: Angulo Gustavo (jesus)
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a morphological representation theory for operators acting in the frequency domain of [MATH]. Equipping the space with the order [MATH] (spectral modulus inequality with phase equality), convolution becomes a morphological erosion and the adjoint dilation is the Wiener inverse filter. A key observation is that spatial translation-invariance is vacuous in the spectral order, replaced structurally by of the operator on spectral moduli. Under this hypothesis we prove the for the Fourier modulus lattice [MATH]: any increasing, USC, positively homogeneous [MATH] decomposes as a supremum of max-times erosions [MATH], indexed by a minimal morphological basis. Three structural corollaries follow: the spectral modulus map [MATH] is an idempotent cross-lattice projection (the morphological analogue of ReLU) that makes depth non-trivial; wavelet scattering coefficients form the canonical dictionary for the basis via Littlewood--Paley density; and spatial pooling is a Fourier erosion, so that pool-then-unpool is the ideal band-pass opening, U-Net skip connections are Fourier top-hat transforms, and strided pooling preserves the morphological structure if and only if the Nyquist condition holds. The framework carries a natural [MATH]-group morphology structure, positioning mathematical morphology as the constructive operator-theoretic complement of spectral bias, scattering, and tropical geometry theories.
tldr: This paper develops a morphological representation theory for operators in the frequency domain, showing that any increasing, USC, positively homogeneous operator decomposes into a supremum of max-times erosions, and uses this to interpret deep learning structures like pooling and skip connections as morphological operations.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a constructive operator-theoretic framework for understanding frequency-domain deep learning operators, complementing spectral bias, scattering, and tropical geometry theories.
method: They equip the space of Fourier modulus with an order based on spectral modulus inequality with phase equality, making convolution a morphological erosion. Then they prove a decomposition theorem for operators under this order, and derive corollaries about ReLU-like projections, wavelet scattering bases, and pooling as Fourier erosion.
result: Key results include: the spectral modulus map is an idempotent cross-lattice projection (morphological analogue of ReLU), wavelet scattering coefficients form a canonical dictionary via Littlewood–Paley density, and pooling/unpooling operations correspond to ideal band-pass openings and top-hat transforms.
conclusion: The framework positions mathematical morphology as a fundamental constructive theory for spectral analysis in deep learning, offering new interpretations and potential design principles for architectures.

title: Minimax Quantile Bounds Via Information Measures
authors: Amedeo Roberto Esposito
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified information-theoretic framework for lower bounding minimax quantiles. The starting point is a loss-adapted Neyman--Pearson metaconverse that bounds the minimax success probability at every loss radius and confidence level. The bound separates the small-ball geometry induced by the prior and loss from the statistical distinguishability of the experiment, and is optimised over an auxiliary output distribution. Different relaxations of this single testing bound yield converses based on \(f\)-informativity, Sibson information \(I_\alpha\), Maximal Leakage, and Amemiya norms. Classical Fano and Le Cam lower bounds are recovered as special cases. The framework also clarifies why different information measures are suited to different recovery criteria. Maximal Leakage is exact for a class of symmetric exact-recovery problems. We use this identity to derive finite-sample bounds on the full minimax exact-recovery risk in the balanced Gaussian weighted stochastic block model, as well as two-sided finite-sample minimax-quantile bounds for low-rank matrix estimation under isotropic bounded-energy noise. For approximate Hamming recovery, we exhibit a heterogeneous binary model in which an optimised finite Sibson order yields a strong converse while the Maximal Leakage specialisation is trivial. Finally, for one-coordinate Poisson localisation, a Bennett-type Young function used through its Amemiya norm recovers the exact success-probability scale, whereas classical Fano and fixed-power relaxations are strictly weaker. These results show that sharp minimax-quantile converses require adapting the information control to both the recovery resolution and the likelihood-ratio tail.
tldr: Develops a unified information-theoretic framework for lower bounding minimax quantiles, recovering classical bounds and enabling sharp converses for various statistical inference problems.
motivation: To provide sharp minimax quantile lower bounds that adapt to recovery criteria and likelihood-ratio tails, unifying and extending existing methods like Fano and Le Cam.
method: Introduces a loss-adapted Neyman-Pearson metaconverse optimized over auxiliary output distributions, with relaxations recovering f-informativity, Sibson information, Maximal Leakage, and Amemiya norms.
result: Framework recovers classical bounds, yields exact minimax exact-recovery risk for balanced Gaussian weighted stochastic block models, two-sided bounds for low-rank matrix estimation, and demonstrates the need for adapted information measures in approximate recovery and Poisson localization.
conclusion: Sharp minimax-quantile converses require adapting the information control to both recovery resolution and likelihood-ratio tails, as no single information measure universally dominates.

title: Exact Scaling Theory Of Social Tipping Phenomena In Finite Populations
authors: Jos\'e F. Fontanari Bianca Y. S. Ishikawa
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Granovetter's threshold model provides a classical framework for social mobilization, where collective action spreads through cascades as individuals join once movement size reaches their personal threshold. Here, we characterize social tipping points-the minimum seed required for global mobilization-using the initial fraction of instigators, [MATH], as a control parameter. For a finite population of size [MATH] with Beta-distributed thresholds [MATH], we present an exact analytical study of the cascade dynamics. By evaluating the asymptotic active fraction [MATH], we map the thermodynamic phase diagram separating partial cascades ([MATH]) from complete mobilization ([MATH]), revealing continuous and discontinuous transition lines that meet seamlessly at a critical endpoint. For interior-peaked distributions ([MATH]), the regimes are separated by a hybrid phase transition combining a first-order discontinuity with second-order bottleneck singularities. Combining exact finite-[MATH] combinatorial formulations with large-deviation theory, we establish how finite-size fluctuations smooth these singularities. For power-law thresholds ([MATH]), the critical scaling window shrinks as [MATH], while the expected inactive fraction vanishes as [MATH] at criticality. For interior-peaked distributions ([MATH]), the order parameter is bimodally distributed: realizations either achieve full mobilization or stall near a bottleneck [MATH]. Excluding fully mobilized trajectories, [MATH] vanishes as [MATH] and the scaling window compresses to [MATH]. Together, these results establish an exact finite-size scaling theory for threshold-driven tipping phenomena.
tldr: The paper develops an exact finite-size scaling theory for social tipping phenomena in finite populations using Granovetter's threshold model with Beta-distributed thresholds, mapping phase diagrams and analyzing critical fluctuations.
motivation: To understand social tipping points—minimum seeds for global mobilization—in finite populations, where exact results beyond mean-field approximations are needed.
method: The authors use exact combinatorial formulations for finite N and large-deviation theory to derive the asymptotic active fraction and characterize phase transitions, including finite-size scaling windows.
result: They reveal continuous and discontinuous transition lines meeting at a critical endpoint, hybrid phase transitions with bottleneck singularities for interior-peaked distributions, and power-law scaling of critical windows.
conclusion: The work establishes an exact finite-size scaling theory for threshold-driven tipping, showing how finite-size effects smooth singularities and influence mobilization outcomes.

title: Impact Of Plasmonic Modes And Thermophysical Properties On The Double-Pulse Structuring Of Highly-Ordered Lipss For Biosensing Applications
authors: G. D. Tsibidis, F. Fraggelakis, P. Lingos, E. Cusworth, V. G. Kravets, A. N. Grigorenko, A. V. Kabashin, E. Stratakis
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fabrication of highly ordered laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) on thin metallic films is dictated, predomaninatly, by a synergy of periodic electromagnetic energy deposition and complex fluid dynamics. In this work, we present a combined experimental and theoretical study on the formation of ultra-regular LIPSS on 32-nm-thick Au films using a double-pulse femtosecond laser scheme. We demonstrate that for thin films, the excitation of coupled Surface Plasmon Polaritons (SPPs) at both interfaces dictates the initial energy distribution. On the othe hand, the final morphology is greatly influenced by hydrodynamical processes. Interestingly, due to the low electron-phonon coupling of Au and the high thermal confinement of the thin film, single-pulse irradiation leads to uncontrolled hydrodynamic instabilities a non uniform topographies. Thus, we demonstrate that a double-pulse approach with an optimized interpulse delay ({\Delta}{\tau}=1.2 ns) effectively controls the melt duration and viscosity, suppressing complex fluid motion and promoting the growth of highly ordered arrays. These structures support narrow surface lattice resonances (SLRs) suitable for high-sensitivity plasmonic biosensing.
tldr: This paper studies double-pulse femtosecond laser structuring of highly ordered LIPSS on thin Au films for plasmonic biosensing, combining experimental and theoretical analysis of SPP excitation and hydrodynamic effects.
motivation: To achieve highly ordered laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) on thin metallic films for biosensing applications, overcoming hydrodynamic instabilities that cause non-uniform topographies.
method: A combined experimental and theoretical approach using a double-pulse femtosecond laser with optimized interpulse delay, coupled with models of coupled surface plasmon polaritons and fluid dynamics.
result: The double-pulse scheme with Δτ=1.2 ns controls melt duration and viscosity, suppressing uncontrolled fluid motion and producing highly ordered arrays that support narrow surface lattice resonances for high-sensitivity biosensing.
conclusion: The double-pulse method effectively fabricates ultra-regular LIPSS on thin Au films, enabling plasmonic biosensing applications.

title: Clifford-efficient Sparse State Preparation For Molecular Wavefunctions
authors: Yingrong Chen, Nathan A. Baker, Rushi Gong, Conrad S. N. Johnston, Brad Lackey, Hongbin Liu, Sasha Schmidt, Yuan Su, David B. Williams-Young, Yinuo Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse quantum state preparation concerns an [MATH]-qubit target state that is a superposition of only [MATH] computational basis states. Existing approaches exploit this sparsity by compressing these [MATH] basis states and their amplitudes onto a smaller set of qubits, called the dense register, before expanding the prepared state to the full register. Rather than relying on the permutation-based compression used in prior work, we exploit affine relationships among the binary configurations over the finite field [MATH] to reduce both the non-Clifford gate count and the ancillary qubit count. Invertible affine transformations over [MATH], comprising Gaussian elimination and all-ones-row removal, first reduce the dense register from [MATH] to the rank [MATH] using only Clifford gates and no ancillary qubits. An optional binary encoding stage then trades additional Toffoli gates and ancillary qubits for further compression to the minimum [MATH] dense qubits needed to represent [MATH] distinct configurations. For chemically relevant wavefunctions, such as those obtained from selected configuration interaction calculations, shared electronic excitation patterns produce many of these affine relationships, enabling substantial Clifford-only compression before binary encoding. Across the molecular benchmarks, our method requires the fewest ancillary qubits among the evaluated sparse state preparation methods while maintaining comparable non-Clifford gate counts when using binary encoding.
tldr: The paper presents a method for efficient sparse quantum state preparation using Clifford gates and affine transformations.
motivation: Sparse state preparation is crucial for quantum simulations, and existing methods require many non-Clifford gates or ancillas.
method: They exploit affine relationships among binary configurations to compress the state onto fewer qubits using Clifford gates, with optional binary encoding to trade Toffoli gates for fewer ancillas.
result: Their method uses fewer ancillas while maintaining comparable non-Clifford gate counts on molecular benchmarks.
conclusion: The approach improves the efficiency of sparse state preparation for chemistry applications.

title: Gas Beam Dump And Power Meter For High Energy Lasers
authors: Harsha Rajesh, Sida Cao, Ke Ou, Devdigvijay Singh, Pierre Michel, Matthew R. Edwards
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gaseous optics exhibit substantially higher laser-induced-damage thresholds than solid materials, enabling high-intensity operation without permanent degradation. In this Letter, we describe a gas-based beam dump and power meter that exploits the strong absorption of ozone in the Hartley band (200-320 nm). We develop and experimentally validate a model for ozone absorption that predicts the propagation length required for complete energy deposition and the resulting gas temperature rise. By calibrating the temperature rise against incident pulse energy, we demonstrate accurate millijoule-scale pulse energy measurements with an all-gas absorber. These results establish gas-phase absorbers as a scalable, debris-free platform for high-damage-threshold beam dumps and energy diagnostics for high-fluence lasers.
tldr: This paper presents a gas-based beam dump and power meter using ozone absorption in the Hartley band for high-energy laser diagnostics.
motivation: Solid materials have limited laser-induced-damage thresholds, necessitating scalable, debris-free alternatives for high-fluence lasers.
method: The authors develop and experimentally validate a model for ozone absorption, predicting propagation length and gas temperature rise, and calibrate temperature rise versus incident pulse energy.
result: They demonstrate accurate millijoule-scale pulse energy measurements with an all-gas absorber.
conclusion: Gas-phase absorbers offer a scalable, debris-free platform for high-damage-threshold beam dumps and energy diagnostics.

title: The Landau-Dirac Operator With Shell Interactions: Self-adjointness And Clustering
authors: Badreddine Benhellal, Vincent Bruneau, Pablo Miranda
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the two-dimensional Dirac operator with constant magnetic field that is perturbed by a combination of electrostatic and Lorentz-scalar delta interactions with variable coefficients supported on a smooth closed curve. Self-adjointness is studied in the so called non critical and critical cases. In the non-critical case the essential spectrum is unchanged - it remains to be the set of the Landau-Dirac levels, the eigenvalues of infinite multiplicity of the unperturbed operator - while in the critical case an additional interval of essential spectrum emerges in the spectral gap containing zero. Our main result concerns the discrete spectrum in the non-critical case: using the pseudodifferential properties of the involved boundary integral operators, we show that the eigenvalues accumulate at each Landau-Dirac level at a rate governed by the logarithmic capacity of the curve. A novel and surprising phenomenon is the change in the side of the accumulation depending on the position relative to the critical value. As a byproduct, clusters of eigenvalues for a family of exterior boundary value problems are obtained via confining couplings; the infinite-mass boundary condition arises as a special case.
tldr: This paper analyzes the spectral properties of a two-dimensional Dirac operator with constant magnetic field perturbed by delta interactions on a curve, revealing eigenvalue accumulation at Landau levels and a novel side change phenomenon.
motivation: The study aims to understand the spectral effects of singular shell interactions on Dirac operators, which are relevant in condensed matter and mathematical physics.
method: The authors use self-adjointness techniques, boundary integral operators, and pseudodifferential calculus to analyze the essential and discrete spectrum in non-critical and critical cases.
result: In the non-critical case, the essential spectrum remains unchanged while eigenvalues accumulate at each Landau level with a rate governed by logarithmic capacity; in the critical case, an additional essential spectrum interval appears, and the side of accumulation changes relative to the critical value.
conclusion: The paper provides a detailed spectral classification and uncovers a surprising side-change in eigenvalue accumulation, contributing to the understanding of Dirac operators with singular perturbations.

title: On Quantum Channels: Extreme Points, Topology, And Categorical Properties
authors: J. M. S. T. Da Silva
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this thesis, quantum channels are studied from the point of view of Mathematics. We studied the CPTP (completely positive trace preserving) and UCPTP channels, the latter being the unital channels. In both cases, the sets are compact convex, so they are the closure of their extreme points. We constructed extreme CPTP maps for every possible rank. We also constructed extreme UCPTP maps with rank 2 for each possible dimension. For ranks of at least 3, we constructed extreme UCPTP maps for many dimensions and ranks. We also proved that the tensor product of extreme CPTP maps is an extreme CPTP map. For UCPTP maps, we proved that the same is not always true, with many counterexamples. It is known that the category of CPTP maps is semicartesian. We add to this a classification of binary products. We proved that products only exist in trivial cases. For binary coproducts, we obtained the dimensions they should have, if they exist. In both cases, topological techniques were used. For this reason, we also investigated the topology of the closure of the set of extreme points of the CPTP maps. Topological invariants can be computed from decompositions of a space such as CW structures. These are a type of decomposition in which the space is expressed as a gluing of balls. In the search for a CW structure for the closure of the set of extreme CPTP maps, we obtained a partial decomposition that resembles a CW structure of the complex projective space.
tldr: This thesis mathematically studies quantum channels (CPTP and UCPTP maps), focusing on extreme points, tensor products, topological properties, and categorical structure.
motivation: To understand the mathematical structure of the convex sets of quantum channels, which is fundamental for quantum information theory but investigated here from a pure mathematics perspective.
method: Constructs extreme maps for various ranks and dimensions, proves properties of tensor products, and uses topological techniques to analyze the closure of extreme points and categorical products/coproducts.
result: Provides constructions of extreme CPTP and UCPTP maps, shows tensor product behavior (extreme for CPTP, not always for UCPTP), classifies binary products and coproducts, and obtains a partial CW-like decomposition for the closure of extreme CPTP maps.
conclusion: The work contributes to the mathematical foundations of quantum channels, but its focus on algebraic topology and category theory is peripheral to the user's research interests in information theory, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.

title: Message Order Selects Opposite Collective Opinions On Laplacian-Cospectral Networks
authors: Ruiwu Niu, Xincheng Shu, Ying Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Receiving the same messages in different orders can change an agent's judgement. We construct a network model in which this local sequence effect determines the final opinion of an entire network. Each agent has a two-level quantum-like state with an expressed opinion and an auxiliary context coordinate that can affect the next update. Two valid update rules of equal strength leave the neutral state unchanged and add no positive or negative opinion bias. Nevertheless, reversing their order gives the exact opinions +0.01 and -0.01 from the same initial state. We place four ordered pairs so that their positive and negative contributions sum to zero but occupy different labelled nodes. After this single input, all cases follow the same nonlinear network rule, which preserves valid states and admits two stable consensuses. We compare two 16-node networks whose complete Laplacian spectra are identical. With every local ingredient fixed, they converge to opposite consensuses. A separate local calculation identifies a specific overlap between the labelled pulse and Laplacian eigenspace projectors that sets the leading displacement of the basin boundary. Rigorous interval arithmetic proves the finite registered example independently. The construction connects message order to collective selection and shows why Laplacian eigenvalues alone do not determine which opinion wins.
tldr: A network model demonstrates that the order of message updates can lead to opposite collective opinions even on Laplacian-cospectral networks, showing that message order selects which consensus emerges.
motivation: To understand how local sequence effects in opinion updates can determine the final collective opinion in a network, and to investigate the role of network topology beyond Laplacian eigenvalues.
method: Each agent is modeled with a two-level quantum-like state and auxiliary context; two update rules of equal strength are applied in different orders. A 16-node network with the same Laplacian spectrum is used, and interval arithmetic provides rigorous verification.
result: Reversing the order of the two update rules yields exact opposite opinions (+0.01 vs -0.01) from the same initial state. Two Laplacian-cospectral networks converge to opposite consensuses despite identical local properties.
conclusion: Message order can be a determining factor for collective selection, and Laplacian eigenvalues alone do not predict which opinion wins.

title: Spectral Anisotropy In Transition Radiation From Biaxial Media
authors: Sven Ebel, Bibi Mary Francis, Min Seok Jang, Brian D. Gerardot, N. Asger Mortensen, Mauro Brotons-Gisbert, Sergii Morozov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In anisotropic optical media, the electromagnetic response depends on the orientation of the optical field relative to the material's principal dielectric axes. While this direction dependence is well understood in conventional optics, it should also influence light-generation processes driven by free electrons. Here, we experimentally observe spectrally anisotropic transition radiation from biaxial van der Waals crystals. Using cathodoluminescence spectroscopy on germanium sulphide (GeS) and molybdenum oxydichloride (MoOCl[MATH]) crystals, we show that the transition-radiation spectra differ along the principal in-plane optical axes. To describe this spectral anisotropy, we develop a thin-film transition-radiation model that reproduces the experimental observations. Our results demonstrate that transition radiation is a sensitive probe of the axis-dependent dielectric response of biaxial optical media and suggest that optical anisotropy can provide an additional degree of freedom for free electron-driven spectroscopy, radiation sources, and transition-radiation-based diagnostics.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes and models spectral anisotropy in transition radiation from biaxial crystals, demonstrating that optical anisotropy affects free-electron-driven light emission.
motivation: To understand how the dielectric anisotropy of biaxial media influences light-generation processes driven by free electrons, which is not well explored in conventional optics.
method: Used cathodoluminescence spectroscopy on germanium sulphide (GeS) and molybdenum oxydichloride (MoOCl2) crystals and developed a thin-film transition radiation model to describe the observed spectra.
result: Observed distinct transition-radiation spectra along the principal in-plane optical axes, and the developed model reproduced the experimental observations.
conclusion: Transition radiation can serve as a sensitive probe of axis-dependent dielectric response, and optical anisotropy offers an additional degree of freedom for free electron-driven spectroscopy and radiation sources.

title: Quantum Wake Dynamics From Distinct Spectroscopic Perturbations
authors: Umesh Kumar, Gonzalo Alvarez, David Alan Tennant, Satoshi Okamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum wake dynamics in quantum magnets have recently been inferred from the dynamical spin structure factor, which probes only a restricted class of local perturbations. Here, we show that resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) selection rules act as an operator filter on fractionalized excitations, producing distinct quantum wakes in the spin-[MATH] Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain. Using explicit real-time evolution of single-spin and spin-conserving bond correlators, we find that the conventional spin response propagates up to the maximum spinon velocity, [MATH], whereas the bond channels concentrate their spectral weight into a slower dominant wake with [MATH], while weaker components remain bounded by the full spinon light cone. The corresponding momentum- and frequency-resolved responses map onto experimentally accessible RIXS channels, demonstrating that different spectroscopic perturbations resolve complementary pathways of many-body propagation beyond the neutron-scattering spin structure factor. Their inelastic spectral weights further provide access to quantum Fisher information, while equal-time bond sum rules connect the same spectroscopic channels to the ground-state energy. Because the same correlators can be prepared and measured on quantum hardware, they also define direct, experimentally anchored benchmarks for quantum simulations, particularly in frustrated and higher-dimensional magnets where controlled classical real-time calculations become challenging.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that RIXS selection rules act as an operator filter, revealing distinct quantum wake dynamics in spin chains, with implications for quantum simulation benchmarks.
motivation: To go beyond the dynamical spin structure factor and explore how different spectroscopic perturbations can resolve complementary many-body propagation pathways in quantum magnets.
method: Using explicit real-time evolution of single-spin and spin-conserving bond correlators in the Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain, the authors map momentum- and frequency-resolved responses onto RIXS channels.
result: They find that spin and bond channels propagate at different velocities, with bond channels showing a slower dominant wake, and connect inelastic spectral weights to quantum Fisher information and equal-time bond sum rules to ground-state energy.
conclusion: Different spectroscopic probes provide complementary views of quantum dynamics and offer experimentally anchored benchmarks for quantum simulations, especially in systems where classical calculations are challenging.

title: Making Sense Of Quantum Technology: Nuance And Comparison In Non-Expert Stakeholder Communication
authors: Floris L\"offler, Lisanne van Veenen, Muhammad Unggul Karami, Julia Cramer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The development of quantum technology (QT) is partly driven by a growing group of non-expert stakeholders, such as policymakers, journalists, and philosophers. Although many of these stakeholders have minimal formal training in quantum science, their communications may greatly influence the QT ecosystem, yet research into it is scarce. We therefore explored the use of framing, metaphors, and jargon by non-expert QT stakeholders through a qualitative content analysis of 12 semi-structured interviews. We found that the stakeholders applied a nuanced lens to QT, typically through socioeconomic framing. Several types of framing previously unidentified in the literature were found, such as explaining QT by comparison with current (emerging) technologies, for example, artificial Intelligence, in terms of capabilities and implementation in society. The use of stakeholder desiderata in such research was also found to be subsidiary to the stakeholder's occupation. This explorative study is meant to serve as a starting point for future studies of this stakeholder group.
tldr: This paper qualitatively analyzes how non-expert stakeholders communicate about quantum technology, using framing and metaphors, finding a nuanced socioeconomic perspective but no technical relevance to quantum information research.
motivation: To understand how non-expert stakeholders like policymakers and journalists communicate about quantum technology, given their influence on the ecosystem but lack of formal training.
method: Qualitative content analysis of 12 semi-structured interviews with non-expert stakeholders.
result: Stakeholders use socioeconomic framing and comparisons with other technologies like AI, revealing previously unidentified framing types.
conclusion: This exploratory study serves as a starting point for future research on non-expert stakeholder communication in quantum technology.

title: Bethe-root Configurations And Spectral Degeneracy In The Open Xxz Chain With Degenerate Boundaries
authors: Shizhang Wu, Shu Chen, Junpeng Cao, Xin Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structure of Bethe-root configurations in the spin-1/2 XXZ chain with degenerate open boundaries. The physical solutions of the Bethe Ansatz equations are classified into three types in the fully degenerate case and two types in the partially degenerate case, for which we propose counting formulas for the number of physical solution sets of each type. Furthermore, we observe spectral degeneracies in the fully degenerate case and show that they can be naturally explained by the presence of specific phantom strings in the Bethe roots. The classification and resulting spectral degeneracies in the diagonal limit are also discussed.
tldr: 该论文研究了带简并边界的开放XXZ链中Bethe根结构的分类和谱简并，提出了物理解集计数公式并解释了谱简并的起源。
motivation: 理解开放边界条件下可积自旋链的Bethe根结构和简并性质，以深入理解量子可积模型的谱结构。
method: 通过分析Bethe ansatz方程，在完全和部分简并边界条件下对物理解进行分类，推导计数公式，并利用phantom strings解释谱简并。
result: 在完全简并情况下识别出三种类型的解，部分简并时有两种，给出了计数公式，并展示了phantom strings导致谱简并。
conclusion: 该分类和谱简并的机制在开放边界XXZ链中成立，并在对角极限下也适用。

title: Attosecond Transient Polarimetry
authors: Nicola Mayer, Kylie Gannan, Stephen R Leone, Lauren B Drescher
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce elliptical-dichroic attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (eDATAS), an ultrafast attosecond spectroscopy technique in which an atomic gas is probed by elliptically polarized attosecond and near-infrared pulses with an arbitrary angle between the polarization ellipses and a varying time-delay. Using perturbation theory, we show that the transient absorption signal factorizes into form factors whose dependence on pulse ellipticities and polarization-ellipse orientations are governed entirely by dipole selection rules: ellipticity sets the amplitudes of the interfering multiphoton pathways, while the relative orientations of the ellipses control the phase. We reinterpret circular- and linear-dichroic attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy as limiting cases of eDATAS, and validate the theory through an eDATAS measurement in helium, finding excellent agreement. Finally, we demonstrate that eDATAS can also serve as an in situ measurement of the polarization state of the XUV field, avoiding the need for a dedicated XUV polarimeter.
tldr: Introduces elliptical-dichroic attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (eDATAS) for studying dipole selection rules and characterizing XUV polarization.
motivation: To advance attosecond spectroscopy by probing light-matter interactions with elliptically polarized pulses and to provide an in situ polarimetry method.
method: Develops a perturbation theory factorization of the transient absorption signal based on pulse ellipticity and relative ellipse orientations, validated experimentally in helium.
result: Theory and experiment agree excellently; eDATAS also serves as an in situ XUV polarimeter.
conclusion: eDATAS is a versatile tool for attosecond science, enabling both fundamental studies and practical polarization measurements.

title: Spin Models With Critical Ground Space Degeneracy From Lie Algebra Relations
authors: Andras Molnar, Efekan K\"okc\"u, Norbert Schuch, Bojko N. Bakalov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an [MATH]-symmetric spin model derived from the algebraic structure of [MATH]: It is obtained as the nearest-neighbor parent Hamiltonian of a Matrix Product State (MPS) built from the generators of the Lie algebra [MATH] and the identity matrix, and therefore encodes the quadratic relations of the Lie algebra. We characterize the ground space structure of the resulting model and show that for open boundary conditions (OBC), it exhibits a quadratic ground space degeneracy, given by one irreducible representation (irrep) of each odd dimension (integer spin). For periodic boundary conditions (PBC), it has a linear ground space degeneracy, consisting of a singlet --- namely, the MPS underlying the model --- and a ferromagnet (the irrep with maximal spin), and thus exhibits gapless excitations. We also generalize the construction and the analysis of the OBC ground space to [MATH] and other compact simple Lie groups. The MPS on which the model is based is an injective MPS, and therefore, its 3-site parent Hamiltonian has a unique ground space and is gapped. The observed critical behavior thus has its origin in the small parent Hamiltonian considered. The model's algebraic ground space scaling thus provides an example distinct from that reported in (Schuch et al., 2025, arXiv:2503.10767), where it was shown that small parent Hamiltonians of injective MPS generically have unique ground states, and examples with an exponential ground space degeneracy were given.
tldr: Introduces a spin model from Lie algebra relations that exhibits critical ground space degeneracy, constructed as a parent Hamiltonian of a Matrix Product State.
motivation: To explore ground space degeneracy arising from algebraic structures and to provide a case distinct from generic injective MPS parent Hamiltonians.
method: Constructs a nearest-neighbor parent Hamiltonian from an MPS built with Lie algebra generators and identity, then analyzes ground states under open and periodic boundary conditions.
result: Shows quadratic degeneracy for OBC (odd-dimensional irreps) and linear degeneracy for PBC (singlet plus ferromagnet), with gapless excitations; generalizes to other simple Lie groups.
conclusion: Demonstrates that the algebraic structure leads to non-generic ground space scaling, indicating that small parent Hamiltonians can have non-unique ground spaces beyond exponential cases.

title: Characterizing Multimode Effects In A Guided Matterwave Gyroscope
authors: Jessica K. Eastman, Ellen Zheng, Stuart S. Szigeti, Simon A. Haine
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate the performance of a compact matterwave vortex gyroscope formed by a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate in a toroidal potential. Unlike conventional atomic gyroscopes that rely on the Sagnac effect, the topological stability of the vortex state yields rotation sensitivity independent of the enclosed area, making the device robust against geometric drifts. Using fully quantum multimode simulations, we quantify two interaction-driven mechanisms that degrade performance: phase diffusion from one-axis-twisting and four-wave mixing from intercomponent scattering. We identify regimes where tuning interaction and trapping parameters produces a trade-off between these effects, and find that reducing the intercomponent scattering length can counterintuitively worsen sensitivity. Finally, we compare the vortex gyroscope to a guided Sagnac interferometer, demonstrating superior scaling, establishing it as a promising candidate for compact precision rotation sensing.
tldr: This paper theoretically analyzes a compact matterwave vortex gyroscope using two-component BEC in a toroidal trap, focusing on multimode effects that degrade sensitivity.
motivation: Conventional atomic gyroscopes rely on the Sagnac effect and are sensitive to geometric drifts. A vortex-based gyroscope offers area-independent rotation sensitivity, but interaction-driven effects like phase diffusion and four-wave mixing may limit performance.
method: The authors use fully quantum multimode simulations to model the two-component BEC gyroscope, quantifying the impact of phase diffusion from one-axis-twisting and four-wave mixing from intercomponent scattering, and comparing it to a guided Sagnac interferometer.
result: They identify trade-offs between interaction and trapping parameters, show that reducing intercomponent scattering can counterintuitively worsen sensitivity, and demonstrate superior scaling of the vortex gyroscope over a guided Sagnac interferometer.
conclusion: The vortex gyroscope is a promising candidate for compact precision rotation sensing, and the study provides insights into optimizing its performance.

title: Anisotropic Dynamical Reconstruction Of Quantum Geometry In Quenched Chern Insulators
authors: Nan Li, Zhiyong Liu, Zhaoxin Liang, Ying Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under unitary dynamics, the Chern number of an evolving quantum state remains conserved even when a quench drives the Hamiltonian across a topological phase transition. In sharp contrast, we reveal an anisotropic dynamical reconstruction of the quantum metric. Following a sudden quench in a two-dimensional Chern insulator, the metric develops a principal frame in which one eigenvalue grows in time whereas the other remains nearly unchanged. At long times, the associated axes align with the energy-gradient direction and the tangent direction of the constant-energy contours of the post-quench Hamiltonian, respectively. This dynamically selected frame is distinct from that of the static post-quench ground-state metric. We identify momentum-dependent relative dynamical phases as its origin: they enhance the distinguishability of neighboring states separated along the energy-gradient direction, while states along an equal-energy contour remain nearly phase locked. Consequently, local and global metric observables acquire characteristic long-time signatures of the post-quench Hamiltonian. Our results establish a nonequilibrium mechanism by which coherent dynamics reorganizes quantum geometry, suggesting new possibilities for its dynamical control.
tldr: The paper reveals that in quenched Chern insulators, the quantum metric undergoes anisotropic dynamical reconstruction, with one eigenvalue growing and the other nearly unchanged, governed by momentum-dependent relative dynamical phases.
motivation: To understand how coherent dynamics reorganizes quantum geometry after a quench, beyond the conserved Chern number.
method: They analyze a sudden quench in a two-dimensional Chern insulator, studying the time evolution of the quantum metric and its eigenvalues, and identify the mechanism via relative dynamical phases.
result: They find that the metric develops a principal frame where one eigenvalue grows while the other stays constant, and the long-time axes align with energy-gradient and constant-energy contour directions, distinct from the static ground-state metric.
conclusion: This establishes a nonequilibrium mechanism for dynamically controlling quantum geometry, suggesting new possibilities for manipulating geometric properties in quantum systems.

title: High-Resolution Speckle-based Single-Pixel Imaging Using Silicon Photonic Non-Redundant Optical Phased Array
authors: Keita Hirashima, Taichiro Fukui, Kento Komatsu, Chun Ren, Yoshiaki Nakano, Takuo Tanemura
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical phased arrays (OPAs) are promising wavefront controlling devices for imaging applications due to their compact and high-speed nature. However, conventional periodic OPAs have a limited spatial resolution, which scales only linearly with the number of optical antennas [MATH]. Here, we experimentally demonstrate high-resolution imaging using a non-redundant OPA (NR-OPA). Due to the non-redundant antenna layout of NR-OPA based on the Costas array, the resolution scales quadratically with [MATH]. Combined with the speckle-based single-pixel imaging (SSPI) scheme, which avoids the need for precise phase calibration, we experimentally achieve a large number of resolvable imaging points exceeding 10,000 using a silicon photonic NR-OPA chip with only [MATH] without sweeping the wavelength. The demonstrated scheme provides a promising route toward mega-pixel imaging by a compact OPA chip with reduced number of phase shifters.
tldr: A silicon photonic non-redundant optical phased array enables high-resolution imaging via speckle-based single-pixel imaging, achieving over 10,000 resolvable points with a compact chip.
motivation: Conventional periodic OPAs have resolution that scales only linearly with antenna number, limiting spatial resolution. The authors aim to improve resolution scaling by using a non-redundant array layout.
method: They design a non-redundant OPA based on a Costas array, which provides quadratic scaling of resolution. They combine this with speckle-based single-pixel imaging (SSPI) to eliminate the need for precise phase calibration.
result: Experimental demonstration shows imaging with >10,000 resolvable points using a silicon photonic chip with a small number of antennas without wavelength sweeping.
conclusion: This approach offers a compact and high-resolution imaging solution, potentially scalable to mega-pixel imaging with reduced phase shifter count.

title: Artificial Anisotropy Induced Bound States In The Continuum For Integrated Photonic Waveguide
authors: Jinzhao Wang, Kunrun Lu, Yuanlin Li, Weiming Yao, Yang Feng, Yidi Cao, Wei Liu, Feng He, Jianan Duan, Yi Zou, Yongkang Dong, Xiaochuan Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable counterintuitive light confinement without radiation loss, providing a powerful foundation for integrated photonic waveguides. However, existing BIC waveguides are predominantly realized through geometry-dependent designs, where the BIC condition is restricted to narrowly defined structural parameters, limiting design flexibility and practical applicability. Artificial optical anisotropy is introduced as a new design paradigm for BIC waveguides. Implemented using subwavelength-grating (SWG) metamaterials, continuously tailorable anisotropy provides an independent degree of freedom for deterministically reshaping the radiative continuum, enabling flexible formation and systematic control of BIC waveguides over a broad design space. Anisotropy-engineered symmetry breaking further enables controllable asymmetric radiation and precisely tailored field leakage. This paradigm transforms BIC waveguides from geometry-constrained structures into an anisotropy-engineered platform, establishing a general framework for programmable radiation engineering and next-generation integrated photonic devices.
tldr: Introduces artificial anisotropy using subwavelength gratings to control bound states in the continuum for flexible integrated photonic waveguides.
motivation: Existing BIC waveguides rely on geometry-dependent designs with restricted parameters; the paper aims to provide a new design paradigm using artificial anisotropy for greater flexibility.
method: Uses subwavelength-grating metamaterials to engineer continuously tailorable anisotropy, which reshapes the radiative continuum and enables BIC formation and control.
result: Achieves flexible formation and systematic control of BIC waveguides over a broad design space, with controllable asymmetric radiation and tailored field leakage.
conclusion: Transforms BIC waveguides into an anisotropy-engineered platform, establishing a general framework for programmable radiation engineering.

title: Degeneracy Beyond The Parity-symmetry Protection In The Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick Model
authors: Jamil Khalouf-Rivera, Miguel Carvajal, Francisco P\'erez-Bernal
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Degeneracy patterns in quantum mechanics stem from the system symmetries. In particular, the broken-symmetry phase in the well-known Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) model is composed of doubly-degenerate states of different parity. In this work, we show that such doublets can exist even if parity is not conserved. For this purpose, our starting point is an anharmonic LMG Hamiltonian with a second-order ground-state quantum phase transition (GSQPT) and a rich spectrum, with two different excited-state quantum phase transitions. The inclusion in the Hamiltonian of a term inducing a first-order GSQPT breaks the parity symmetry but conserving the exponential degeneracy in the energy doublets. We demonstrate that this phenomenon can be traced back to the existence of a [MATH] symmetry (reflection symmetry) in the system's classical limit phase space that leads to an anti-unitary [MATH] symmetry in the quantum system.
tldr: This paper shows that degeneracy doublets in the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model persist even when parity symmetry is broken, due to a classical reflection symmetry inducing an anti-unitary quantum symmetry.
motivation: The paper investigates the origin of degeneracy beyond parity-symmetry protection in the LMG model, aiming to understand how doublets can exist when parity is not conserved.
method: The authors start with an anharmonic LMG Hamiltonian with a second-order ground-state quantum phase transition, then add a term inducing a first-order GSQPT that breaks parity symmetry while conserving exponential degeneracy in energy doublets.
result: They demonstrate that the doublets persist without parity conservation and trace the phenomenon to a reflection symmetry in the classical limit phase space, which leads to an anti-unitary symmetry in the quantum system.
conclusion: The paper reveals a new mechanism for degeneracy based on anti-unitary symmetry, providing insights into symmetry-induced degeneracy in quantum many-body systems.

title: Regularized Summation Of Fourier-Laguerre Series In The Weighted Sup-norm
authors: Y. A. Volynets S. G. Solodky
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of recovering functions defined on the half-line from inexact input information. For the proposed regularizing summation methods based on Laguerre polynomials, we analyze their approximation properties on functions from Wiener classes. We establish conditions under which these methods are stable with respect to small perturbations of the input data and order-optimal not only in accuracy in the weighted [MATH]-norm, but also in the number of Fourier-Laguerre coefficients used.
tldr: This paper presents regularized summation methods based on Fourier-Laguerre series for recovering functions on the half-line from noisy data, analyzing their stability and order-optimality in weighted sup-norm.
motivation: Recovering functions on the half-line from inexact input data is a classic problem; the authors aim to devise methods that are both stable and optimal in accuracy and coefficient usage.
method: The authors propose regularization techniques using Laguerre polynomials and analyze the approximation properties on Wiener classes, establishing conditions for stability and order-optimality.
result: They prove that under certain conditions, the methods are stable with respect to perturbations and achieve order-optimal accuracy in the weighted L∞ norm as well as in the number of Fourier-Laguerre coefficients.
conclusion: The proposed regularized summation methods are stable and optimal for reconstructing functions on the half-line, making them useful for inverse problems and approximation tasks.

title: Quasi-periodicity And Almost Equality Classes
authors: Mikael Pichot
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss the almost stability theorem of Dicks and Dunwoody in the context of probability measure preserving equivalence relations.
tldr: This paper discusses the almost stability theorem of Dicks and Dunwoody in the context of probability measure preserving equivalence relations.
motivation: To extend or analyze stability results for equivalence relations in ergodic theory, potentially connecting to quasi-periodicity and almost equality classes.
method: Likely uses techniques from ergodic theory, descriptive set theory, and Borel equivalence relations to study the structure of measure-preserving equivalence relations.
result: Provides a discussion and possibly new insights into the almost stability theorem as applied to probability measure preserving equivalence relations.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of measure-preserving equivalence relations, but is not relevant to the specified research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Grothendieck Group Of The Level -1 Type D: Gaps In Jin's Proof And A Complete Proof
authors: Morris Jain
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jin recently claims that the distinguished level [MATH] vacuum block of [MATH] realizes the specialized dual affine left-cell module attached to the subregular cell containing [MATH]. We show that the proof of this Grothendieck-group statement contains a gap. We give an explicit counterexample over the discrete valuation ring [MATH], showing that the categorical implication used in the proof is false in general. Consequently, Jin's Theorem~6.3 does not follow from the argument given in his Section~6.2. We then supply a complete replacement proof for the grading-restricted level-[MATH] vacuum block. Combining the classification of simple objects, we prove finite length, construct an injective signed normalized-character map into a completed singular orbit module, and identify its image with the specialized dual subregular left-cell module. Thus the cell-module realization claimed is established for the grading-restricted vacuum block.
tldr: This paper identifies a gap in Jin's proof of a cell-module realization and provides a complete proof for the grading-restricted level-1 vacuum block.
motivation: To correct and complete the claimed result about the specialized dual affine left-cell module attached to the subregular cell.
method: The paper provides a counterexample over a discrete valuation ring to show the categorical implication is false, then supplies a complete replacement proof using classification of simple objects and an injective signed normalized-character map.
result: It proves finite length, constructs an injective map into a completed singular orbit module, and identifies the image with the specialized dual subregular left-cell module.
conclusion: The cell-module realization is established for the grading-restricted vacuum block, correcting the previous proof.

title: Lattice Vertex Algebras Of Type Ade Over Fields Of Prime Characteristic And Their Representations
authors: Hongju Zhao Qiang Mu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study lattice vertex algebras of type ADE over an algebraically closed field [MATH] of prime characteristic [MATH] and their representations. Let [MATH] be a root lattice of type ADE, and [MATH] the Gram matrix of [MATH]. title: Characterization Of Frame-Related Sequences On Semi-Hilbert Spaces
authors: P. Sam Johnson Hemalatha M
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] and [MATH] be positive bounded operators. We investigate reduced weighted adjoints of densely defined closable operators and use them to develop frame-type systems in the semi-Hilbert spaces induced by [MATH] and [MATH]. Closedness, boundedness, range behavior, and algebraic properties of the [MATH]-adjoint are established, with particular attention to sums, products, and double adjoints in the unbounded setting. We then study the associated [MATH]-analysis, [MATH]-synthesis, and [MATH]-frame operators. Operator-theoretic characterizations of [MATH]-Bessel sequences, [MATH]-lower semi-frames, and [MATH]-frames are obtained, and examples show that several natural weighted-adjoint identities may hold only as proper inclusions. A Douglas-type range characterization for [MATH]-frames is also derived.

motivation: The authors aim to generalize frame theory to more general Hilbert space settings with two weights, motivated by applications in operator theory and signal processing.
method: They introduce reduced weighted adjoints of densely defined closable operators and use them to define analysis, synthesis, and frame operators in semi-Hilbert spaces.
result: They characterize Bessel sequences, lower semi-frames, and frames in this setting, and show that some natural identities hold only as proper inclusions, along with a Douglas-type range characterization.
conclusion: The work extends classical frame theory to a broader operator-theoretic framework, offering new tools for analysis in semi-Hilbert spaces.

title: Time-Inconsistent MDPs With Entropy Regularization: Equilibrium Existence And Policy Iteration
authors: Zhenhua Wang Fengyuan Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study infinite-horizon time-inconsistent Markov decision processes with a countably infinite state space and unbounded reward functions. The reward is allowed to depend explicitly on the initial time and initial state, thereby accommodating general sources of time inconsistency. We seek relaxed feedback equilibria, and our approach is based on entropy regularization and weighted functional analytic methods. With entropy regularization, we characterize a regular relaxed equilibrium through a fixed-point operator. By introducing two weight functions with distinct roles, one controlling the growth of rewards and values and the other defining the ambient weighted space, we construct a compact invariant set under a product topology and apply the Schauder-Tychonoff fixed-point theorem to establish existence of regularized equilibria. Importantly, the invariant set can be chosen uniformly for small entropy weight [MATH]. We then let [MATH] and show, through compactness, concentration of Gibbs policies, and uniform-integrability arguments, that a subsequential limit is a relaxed equilibrium of the original unregularized problem. We further study a policy iteration algorithm (PIA) for the entropy-regularized equilibrium problem. Under a weighted-discounting structure and sufficiently strong discounting, we establish exponential convergence and uniqueness of the regularized equilibrium in a suitable weighted Banach space. Combining the policy-iteration error with a quantitative soft-max approximation bound, we show that the iterated policies constitute weighted [MATH]-equilibria for the original unregularized problem and derive an explicit regret estimate. A numerical example illustrating the convergence of PIA under strong discounting and a counterexample demonstrating its failure under weak discounting are also provided.
tldr: This paper studies time-inconsistent Markov decision processes with entropy regularization, establishing existence of relaxed equilibria and a policy iteration algorithm with convergence guarantees.
motivation: Time-inconsistent MDPs arise when rewards depend on the initial state and time, requiring novel equilibrium concepts; the paper aims to provide rigorous theoretical foundations for such problems.
method: The authors use entropy regularization to define a regularized equilibrium characterized by a fixed-point operator, then apply Schauder-Tychonoff fixed-point theorem and compactness arguments. They also analyze a policy iteration algorithm in a weighted Banach space.
result: They prove existence of regularized equilibria, show convergence to equilibria of the unregularized problem as the entropy weight approaches zero, and derive exponential convergence of policy iteration under strong discounting with explicit regret bounds.
