conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive theoretical treatment of entropy-regularized time-inconsistent MDPs, offering both existence results and algorithmic guarantees, with a numerical example illustrating convergence.

title: Uncertainty Principles For The Short-Time Fourier Transform On The Heisenberg Group
authors: Arvish Dabra, Aparajita Dasgupta, Prerna Gulia
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a systematic theory of uncertainty principles for the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) on the Heisenberg group. Building on recent developments in modulation spaces and time-frequency analysis on the Heisenberg group introduced by Fischer et al. and later by Biswas-Thangavelu, we establish noncommutative analogues of several fundamental uncertainty principles in time-frequency analysis, including Benedicks' theorem, the Donoho-Stark uncertainty principle, and Lieb's inequality. As a consequence of Lieb's inequality, we derive an entropy-based uncertainty principle of Hirschman type. We further establish a Heisenberg-type uncertainty inequality and local uncertainty principles in the spirit of Price. In addition, we prove a Beurling-Hardy-type theorem that captures the interplay between decay and phase-space localization. Finally, we investigate decay properties of the STFT and their implications for time-frequency concentration. These results extend a broad spectrum of classical uncertainty phenomena from the Euclidean setting to the Heisenberg group, highlighting the role of noncommutative harmonic analysis in the study of phase-space localization.
tldr: Develops systematic uncertainty principles for the short-time Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group, extending classical time-frequency analysis to a noncommutative setting.
motivation: The paper aims to extend classical uncertainty principles to the Heisenberg group, leveraging recent developments in modulation spaces and time-frequency analysis.
method: Builds on prior work by Fischer et al. and Biswas-Thangavelu, establishing analogues of Benedicks, Donoho-Stark, Lieb, Heisenberg, local, and Beurling-Hardy type inequalities.
result: Derives noncommutative versions of several fundamental uncertainty principles, including an entropy-based Hirschman principle, and investigates decay properties of the STFT.
conclusion: The results highlight the role of noncommutative harmonic analysis in phase-space localization, but are purely mathematical without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Bridging Semantics And Behavior: An Agent-Based Evolutionary Model Of Topic Competition With BERTopic
authors: Blekanov I., Gubar E., Fan X
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how information spreads and opinions evolve on social media is a core challenge in computational social science. Users constantly face competing topics, yet their decisions to engage are shaped by social learning, perceived utility, and cognitive limits. Traditional models often separate content from behavior, missing how individual cognition and social interaction jointly drive large-scale discourse. We propose a language-independent computational framework that bridges semantic topic modeling with evolutionary game theory and agent-based simulation. Using BERTopic, we extract coherent topics from a large Weibo dataset. We then quantify engagement through a unified metric based on likes, comments, and reposts. In NetLogo, agents update topic preferences via local imitation, guided by payoff comparisons and behavioral noise---mirroring real-world bounded rationality. Tests on two real-world datasets show that our model successfully replicates observed topic diffusion trends. It highlights how social learning frequency and payoff sensitivity shape public attention. Our results demonstrate that micro-level mechanisms---imitation and noise-tolerant choice---can produce emergent macro-level patterns. This work contributes to human-computer interaction by linking semantic analysis with behavioral simulation, offering insights into the cognitive and social foundations of online collective behavior. The framework also has practical potential for misinformation resilience, opinion forecasting, and adaptive content curation.
tldr: This paper proposes a computational framework combining BERTopic semantic topic modeling with evolutionary game theory and agent-based simulation to model topic competition on social media, validated on real-world Weibo data.
motivation: Traditional models separate content from behavior, missing how individual cognition and social interaction jointly drive large-scale discourse; a unified framework is needed to bridge semantics and behavior.
method: The framework uses BERTopic to extract topics from a Weibo dataset, defines an engagement metric based on likes/comments/reposts, and simulates agent behavior in NetLogo with local imitation, payoff comparison, and behavioral noise.
result: Tests on two real-world datasets show the model replicates observed topic diffusion trends, and micro-level imitation and noise-tolerant choice produce emergent macro-level patterns.
conclusion: The work contributes to human-computer interaction by linking semantic analysis with behavioral simulation, offering insights into online collective behavior and potential applications in misinformation resilience, opinion forecasting, and content curation.

title: Optimal Sensor Placement For Output Estimation Using An Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm With Pre-filter
authors: R. P. P. F. Goetz, Y. Dwaraga, N. van de Wouw, T. Oomen, M. M. J. van de Wal, B. Sharif, H. J. Zwart
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensor placement for maximizing the estimation performance of the Kalman filter is an NP-hard optimization problem. Furthermore, its feasible set grows combinatorially with the candidate locations and the number of sensors. In this paper, we study this sensor placement problem for a 3D thermoelastic system modelled as a discrete-time linear stochastic model. We use the Novel Binary Artificial Bee Colony (NBABC) algorithm with a Gramian-based pre-filter to reduce the computational complexity. Our results show the efficiency and the fast convergence of the proposed approach.
tldr: This paper presents an optimal sensor placement method for a 3D thermoelastic system using an artificial bee colony algorithm with a Gramian-based pre-filter to enhance Kalman filter estimation performance.
motivation: Sensor placement for output estimation is NP-hard and combinatorially complex, necessitating efficient optimization approaches. The aim is to reduce computational burden while maintaining estimation accuracy.
method: The authors employ the Novel Binary Artificial Bee Colony (NBABC) algorithm with a Gramian-based pre-filter to solve the sensor placement problem for a discrete-time linear stochastic model of a 3D thermoelastic system.
result: The proposed approach demonstrates efficiency and fast convergence in simulations, indicating its effectiveness for the specific sensor placement task.
conclusion: The combination of NBABC with a pre-filter provides a promising solution for optimal sensor placement in thermoelastic systems, though relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is absent.

title: On The Horizon Problem Over The Product Of Self-similar Fractals
authors: Gurubachan, S. Verma, V. V. M. S. Chandramouli
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we first investigate the box dimension results for the graphs of continuous functions defined on the product of two self-similar fractals ({}s), where the fractal {} satisfies the open set condition. Following this, we manifest the existence of a prevalent surface, defined by a continuous function over the product of two {}s, that satisfies the horizon property (associated with the box dimension), i.e., the box dimension of the prevalent surface is greater than that of its horizon up to a constant {\eta}, where {\eta} is the box dimension of the self-similar fractal {}.
tldr: This paper studies the box dimension of graphs of continuous functions on products of self-similar fractals and demonstrates the existence of prevalent surfaces satisfying a certain horizon property.
motivation: The horizon problem concerns the relationship between the dimension of a surface and its graph, and this paper extends such analysis to products of self-similar fractals.
method: The authors employ techniques from fractal geometry, including the open set condition and box dimension calculations, to analyze the graphs of continuous functions on fractal product domains.
result: They establish box dimension results for these graphs and prove that there exists a prevalent surface over the product of two self-similar fractals such that its box dimension exceeds that of its horizon by the fractal's box dimension constant.
conclusion: The work contributes to the mathematical theory of fractal dimensions and prevalent behavior, but has no apparent connection to quantum information or related fields.

title: A Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Method For Wave Propagation In Elastic Beam Networks
authors: Moritz Hauck (karlsruhe Institute Of Technology), Joseph Holten (karlsruhe Institute Of Technology), Axel M{\aa}lqvist (chalmers University Of Technology And University Of Gothenburg), Andreas Rupp (saarland University), Lucia Swoboda
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the numerical solution of elastic wave propagation on networks, modeled by elastodynamic equations posed on each edge, coupled at the nodes through suitable transmission conditions. We propose and analyze a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method that exploits the network structure to reduce the global problem at each time step to a linear system whose size depends only on the number of network nodes and not on the polynomial degree of the discretization. Combining it with an energy-conservative implicit time discretization, we derive a priori error estimates of optimal order in space and time. The implicit time discretization avoids the severe CFL restriction caused by the large variation in fiber segment lengths. To efficiently solve the resulting, typically ill-conditioned global system, we introduce a two-level overlapping additive Schwarz preconditioner. Under suitable assumptions on the network, we establish uniform convergence of the resulting preconditioned conjugate gradient method. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper presents a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method for simulating elastic wave propagation on beam networks, with optimal error estimates and an efficient preconditioner.
motivation: Simulating wave propagation in beam networks is important in structural mechanics, and existing methods suffer from severe CFL restrictions due to varying segment lengths.
method: The authors combine a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin spatial discretization with an energy-conservative implicit time integrator, reducing the global system to a node-based linear system, and introduce a two-level overlapping additive Schwarz preconditioner for efficient PCG solution.
result: They derive a priori error estimates of optimal order in space and time and prove uniform convergence of the preconditioned conjugate gradient method under suitable assumptions, confirmed by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed method provides an efficient and provably convergent numerical scheme for wave propagation in elastic beam networks, overcoming CFL limitations.

title: Information Geometry Of Gradient Flows
authors: Shintaro Yoshizawa
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Taking classical information geometry as its point of departure, this paper investigates, through gradient flows, how dually flat geometry extends beyond regular convexity, non-degeneracy, and smoothness. The regular theory is developed from the log-determinant potential on positive definite Gram matrices, establishing its Legendre dual, Fisher--Rao metric, Bregman divergence, and generalized Pythagorean theorem. We connect this framework to Craig--Sakamoto deformation, Wolfe duality, and, via Yoshizawa's embedding, Brockett--Bloch--Ratiu double-bracket flows, linking isospectral dynamics, Stiefel optimization, and component learning. The Bures--Wasserstein geometry provides a complementary gradient-flow structure. The singular theory emerges from boundary behavior: difference-of-convex deformations produce indefinite or degenerate Hessians while retaining pseudo-Hessian, dually flat, Legendre-self-dual structures. Newton flows exhibit finite-time collapse or {\L}ojasiewicz-controlled convergence near non-Morse critical sets. Fisher-metric degeneracies on the Birkhoff polytope and elliptic-curve moduli are resolved by explicit blow-ups, yielding a birationally invariant exponential decay law. We further derive a closed-form Kirillov Jacobian and introduce cross curvature as a spectral diagnostic of local escape rates, including a new Box--Cox interpolation. Reproducible numerical experiments support the closed-form results. Rather than claiming a completed theory, the paper provides foundations for singular information geometry centered on degenerate pencils, indefinite dual flatness, blow-up geometry, and {\L}ojasiewicz-type convergence.
tldr: This paper extends dually flat information geometry to singular, non-convex, and degenerate settings via gradient flows, connecting to matrix optimization and blow-up geometry.
motivation: To understand how the regular theory of information geometry, based on convexity and smoothness, can be generalized to boundary and degenerate cases.
method: Uses gradient flows, Legendre duality, Bures–Wasserstein geometry, and explicit blow-ups to handle metric degeneracies and indefinite Hessians.
result: Provides foundations for singular information geometry, including indefinite dual flatness, Lojasiewicz-type convergence, and a closed-form Kirillov Jacobian, supported by numerical experiments.
conclusion: Establishes a foundational framework for singular information geometry without claiming a completed theory, emphasizing degenerate pencils and blow-up geometry.

title: Explicit Exposure Of Haar Measure
authors: Yixuan Huang, Oliver Jenkinson, Zhiqiang Li, Hang Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve the problem of explicitly constructing a continuous function whose unique maximizing measure for the doubling map is Lebesgue measure. More generally, given a nontrivial compact metrizable abelian group and a continuous surjective endomorphism for which normalised Haar measure is ergodic, we explicitly construct a continuous function on the group for which Haar measure is the unique invariant maximizing measure. The function is the uniform limit of a recursively defined sequence of trigonometric polynomials with rational coefficients; every parameter of the recursion is given by a closed formula, every step is exact, and the rate of convergence is explicit. In specific cases, we further obtain a uniformly convergent Fourier expansion in the classical frequency order, each of whose coefficients is rational and computable exactly, by a finite procedure.
tldr: The paper explicitly constructs a continuous function whose unique maximizing measure is the Haar measure for certain ergodic endomorphisms on compact abelian groups.
motivation: To solve the problem of explicitly constructing such functions, which had previously only been known in existence.
method: The function is defined as a uniform limit of recursively defined trigonometric polynomials with rational coefficients, with closed-form recursion parameters and explicit convergence rate.
result: Provides an explicit construction for the doubling map and generalizes to any ergodic endomorphism on a nontrivial compact metrizable abelian group, with computable Fourier coefficients in specific cases.
conclusion: The construction is fully explicit and exact, marking a significant advance in the theory of maximizing measures.

title: The First Tight Classification Of Skew-constacyclic Codes Over Finite Fields
authors: Susanne Pumluen Monica Nevins
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We parametrize the isometry and equivalence classes of skew constacyclic codes over a finite field by classifying the corresponding classes of their ambient rings, and present algorithms for the parametrizations. We achieve a tight classification by taking all possible Hamming-weight preserving isomorphisms between their ambient Petit rings into account. We also count the number of equivalence classes of these rings. We present many examples where isometry is a strictly stronger relation than equivalence, that is, codes that are isometric but not equivalent.
tldr: The paper classifies skew constacyclic codes over finite fields by considering Hamming-weight preserving isomorphisms between their ambient rings, providing a tight classification and algorithms for parametrization.
motivation: To achieve a tight classification that distinguishes isometry from equivalence classes for skew constacyclic codes.
method: Parametrizes isometry and equivalence classes by classifying their ambient Petit rings, incorporating all Hamming-weight preserving isomorphisms, and counting equivalence classes of rings.
result: Presents algorithms for parametrization and examples showing isometry is strictly stronger than equivalence for these codes.
conclusion: The classification is tight and includes a count of equivalence classes, clarifying the relationship between isometry and equivalence for skew constacyclic codes.

title: Cohomological Reduction For Fiber-Contracting Extensions:From Subcohomology To Thermodynamic Formalism
authors: Giovane Ferreira
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a reduction and transfer framework for cohomological, variational, and thermodynamic problems in fiber-contracting extensions of local homeomorphisms. Under uniform contraction along the fibers and the existence of a continuous global section, every H\"older potential admits the explicit decomposition \[ \varphi=\psi\circ\pi+u-u\circ F, \] where [MATH] is defined on the quotient and [MATH] is obtained by a uniformly convergent fiberwise series. We give quantitative criteria for continuity and H\"older regularity and use the reduction to transfer subcohomological and Livic-type statements from the quotient to the extension. We prove that invariant measures on the extension and quotient are in bijection, invariant averages are preserved, and the fibers have zero relative topological entropy. Consequently, metric entropy, ergodic optimization, pressure, minimizing measures, and equilibrium states correspond. We further establish weak Gibbs transfer under subexponential comparison of Bowen-ball masses and prove blockwise Bowen sequential weak Gibbs transfer along prescribed point-dependent Gibbs times; under uniformly bounded sequential mass distortion, the strong Bowen sequential Gibbs property is preserved. Concrete criteria for Bowen-ball comparability are provided. Finally, affine and symbolic contracting skew-products illustrate the framework, including the explicit reduction \[ \varphi(x,y)=g(x)+by \quad\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\quad \psi(x)=g(x)+{1-a}\rho(x) \] for [MATH], [MATH].
tldr: The paper develops a reduction framework for cohomological and thermodynamic problems in fiber-contracting extensions, showing that invariant measures and thermodynamic quantities on the extension correspond to those on the quotient.
motivation: The work aims to simplify the analysis of thermodynamic formalism in fiber-contracting extensions by reducing problems to a quotient system.
method: The author establishes explicit decompositions of potentials and shows bijections between invariant measures, preserving entropy and pressure.
result: They prove that metric entropy, pressure, and equilibrium states correspond between the extension and quotient, and establish Gibbs transfer properties.
conclusion: The framework provides a general tool for studying thermodynamic formalism in contracting extensions, with applications to affine and symbolic systems.

title: Shared Physics Responses Recover Hidden Rankings In Neural Operator Libraries
authors: Fujun Liu Hanbing Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Selecting the optimal neural-operator prediction during deployment is challenging when high-fidelity reference solutions are unavailable. We demonstrate that under a squared Hilbert-space loss, ranking a finite model library depends strictly on the low-dimensional span of candidate differences, allowing us to score all models simultaneously using a single anchor-based linearized response of the governing equation. This shared physical diagnostic accurately recovered over 99.6\% of pairwise preferences and 99.0\% of optimal checkpoints across diverse Fourier and convolutional operator libraries for fluid, reaction-diffusion, and wave dynamics. Furthermore, the corrected physical proxy frequently outperformed the best individual candidates, and we establish computable sufficient conditions that rigorously certify exact decisions for strongly monotone discretizations. By exploiting the local dynamical response rather than raw defect magnitude, this framework enables the reliable and highly efficient deployment of scientific surrogates without requiring ground-truth data.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to rank neural operator models without ground truth by using a linearized response of the governing equation, achieving high accuracy in selecting optimal surrogates.
motivation: Selecting the best neural-operator prediction during deployment is challenging when high-fidelity reference solutions are unavailable, motivating the need for a reliable ranking approach.
method: The authors show that under a squared Hilbert-space loss, ranking a finite model library depends on the low-dimensional span of candidate differences, and they use an anchor-based linearized response to score all models simultaneously.
result: The shared physical diagnostic recovered over 99.6% of pairwise preferences and 99.0% of optimal checkpoints across diverse Fourier and convolutional operator libraries for fluid, reaction-diffusion, and wave dynamics, and often outperformed the best candidates.
conclusion: By exploiting local dynamical response rather than raw defect magnitude, the framework enables reliable and efficient deployment of scientific surrogates without requiring ground-truth data.

title: Four-Entropic Matroids Are Quaternary
authors: Shahram Khazaei Mohammad Hossein Kalantari
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20553v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A matroid is [MATH]-entropic if its rank function, multiplied by [MATH], is the joint-entropy function of random variables on a four-element alphabet. We prove that a matroid is [MATH]-entropic if and only if it is representable over [MATH]. The proof combines minor closure and the excluded-minor characterization of quaternary matroids with structural properties of quasigroups of order four. Thus arbitrary four-symbol partition representations yield no matroids beyond the quaternary ones. As an application, every access structure admitting an ideal perfect scheme with a uniform four-symbol secret and four-symbol active shares also admits an ideal [MATH]-linear scheme.
tldr: Proves that four-entropic matroids are exactly quaternary representable matroids.
motivation: To characterize matroids arising from joint entropy functions on a four-element alphabet and link them to linear representability.
method: Uses minor closure, excluded-minor characterization of quaternary matroids, and quasigroup properties.
result: Four-entropic matroids are precisely the matroids representable over GF(4).
conclusion: This establishes that access structures with ideal perfect schemes using four-symbol alphabets also admit ideal linear schemes.

title: A Characterization Of The Reversibility Of Linear Cellular Automata
authors: Alonso Castillo-Ramirez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let [MATH] be a group, let [MATH] be a field, and let [MATH] be a [MATH]-vector space. We prove that there exists a bijective linear cellular automaton [MATH] whose inverse is not a cellular automaton if and only if [MATH] is not locally finite and [MATH]. This answers an open problem proposed by T. Ceccherini-Silberstein and M. Coornaert.
tldr: This paper provides a complete characterization of when a bijective linear cellular automaton over a vector space configuration has an inverse that is not a cellular automaton, answering an open question.
motivation: Understanding the reversibility of cellular automata is a fundamental problem; the author addresses a specific open question about the existence of bijective linear CAs whose inverses are not themselves CAs.
method: The proof uses algebraic methods, analyzing the structure of linear cellular automata on A^G for a group G and vector space A, and deriving conditions based on the local finiteness of G.
result: It is shown that such a transformation exists if and only if G is not locally finite and A satisfies a certain (likely infinite-dimensional) condition, thereby resolving the open problem.
conclusion: The characterization clarifies the algebraic constraints on reversibility of linear cellular automata, contributing to the theoretical foundation of cellular automata.

title: Keyed Provenance Watermarking With Complementary Lattice-Based Secure Aggregation For Federated Learning
authors: Xinyun Liu, Zhi Lu, Yu Chen, Ronghua Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) is vulnerable to multi-level attacks. However, existing methods address them separately, leaving FL exposed to data leakage, unauthorized reuse, and malicious gradient manipulation. In this work, we propose an FL framework that couples keyed context-provenance watermarking with verifiable lattice-based secure aggregation of Real-World Anchored Watermarking and Lattice-Based Zero-Knowledge Secure Aggregation. At the data layer, we propose a Kerckhoffs-compliant scheme that utilizes Physical Anchor Metadata (PAM) to ensure data provenance. PAM is defined as a context-provenance token derived from trusted infrastructure data (time, location, and server ID) and then subjected to a keyed HMAC-SHA-256 transformation to produce a watermark payload that cannot be generated without the client's secret key. We further design FMGAN, a GAN-based robust image watermarking framework that embeds this transformed payload using a feature fusion module and a Mamba-guided linear attention mechanism. At the computation layer, we adopt a lattice-based zero-knowledge secure aggregation (LZKSA) protocol that verifies key correctness, L2 norm bounds, and cosine similarity constraints over committed gradients without revealing private updates. The RLWE-based design guarantees post-quantum security. Extensive experiments validate the complementary protection of the two layers under composite attack scenarios. To our knowledge, no prior verification workflow has jointly evaluated both layers in a hybrid, end-to-end trustworthy FL framework.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated learning framework that combines keyed provenance watermarking with lattice-based secure aggregation to address data leakage, unauthorized reuse, and gradient manipulation.
motivation: Federated learning is vulnerable to multi-level attacks, but existing defenses handle them separately, leaving systems exposed. The authors aim to provide a unified solution.
method: The framework uses Physical Anchor Metadata to generate watermarks via HMAC-SHA-256, embeds them with a GAN-based image watermarking method (FMGAN), and employs lattice-based zero-knowledge secure aggregation (LZKSA) for gradient verification.
result: Extensive experiments demonstrate the complementary protection of the two layers under composite attack scenarios.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid framework offers an end-to-end trustworthy federated learning approach, though it is not directly related to the specified research interests.

title: More Granular, Less Trust: Enforcing Intra-Process Isolation With Arm Cca In An Untrusted Management Environment
authors: Shiqi Liu, Zhouqi Jiang, Jie Wang, Wei Zhou, Kun Sun, Zhaohui Chen, Yulai Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the increasing adoption of confidential computing, security-sensitive applications are often deployed in confidential virtual machines (CVMs), which reduce reliance on third-party cloud providers. However, privilege attacks originating from the OS remain a significant threat in these environments. Existing finer-grained isolation schemes, such as SHELTER, provide process-level protection but are still vulnerable to intraprocess attacks and potential collusion between the OS and intra-process adversaries. Many current intra-process isolation techniques continue to depend on the OS to manage and enforce isolation domains, leading to a large Trusted Computing Base (TCB). This gap highlights the need for more granular, less trust-dependent confidential computing solutions. In this paper, we present CCAegis, a system that extends the Arm Confidential Compute Architecture (CCA) to enforce intra-process isolation of sensitive data and operations, safeguarding them from both intraprocess adversaries and the OS. We employ static analysis to track the flow of sensitive data and identify functions that handle such data. Permission-switching instructions are inserted at the function call and return points, adjusting permissions via the Granule Protection Table (GPT) to ensure that only designated functions can access the isolated data. Notably, CCAegis places trust solely in the Secure Monitor, which configures the GPTs and manages domain switching, thereby minimizing the TCB. We implemented CCAegis on both an official emulator and a real development board to assess its performance. Our experimental results show that CCAegis effectively isolates sensitive data and operations, with performance overheads ranging from 1.01x to 1.43x compared to the original version across real-world cryptographic workloads.
tldr: This paper presents CCAegis, a system that uses Arm Confidential Compute Architecture to enforce intra-process isolation, protecting sensitive data from both OS and intra-process attacks.
motivation: Existing confidential computing solutions are vulnerable to OS-level and intra-process attacks, and current intra-process isolation schemes rely on a large trusted computing base. There is a need for more granular isolation with less trust in the OS.
method: CCAegis uses static analysis to track sensitive data flow and inserts permission-switching instructions at function boundaries, adjusting permissions via the Granule Protection Table (GPT) to restrict access solely to designated functions, with trust placed only in the Secure Monitor.
result: Implemented on an emulator and a real development board, CCAegis effectively isolates sensitive data and operations with performance overheads from 1.01x to 1.43x across real-world cryptographic workloads.
conclusion: CCAegis demonstrates that intra-process isolation can be achieved with minimal TCB by leveraging Arm CCA hardware features, offering a practical solution for confidential computing environments.

title: Beyond Explicit Generators: Distribution-Free Linear-Decomposition Attacks On Public-Key Encryption
authors: Ding-Xuan Zhou Ziyan Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear-decomposition attacks can break public-key schemes without recovering the secret algebraic action: when a target public state lies in a known linear span, its decomposition coefficients transfer through the unknown action to reveal the shared value. We study a setting in which the adversary uses only the public sampling-and-evaluation oracle available to honest participants, the induced distribution is arbitrary, and the goal is to attack future ciphertexts rather than recover the full algebraic span. We model public paired samples under a fixed secret linear transport and define the sampled-orbit dimension as the effective dimension of the encryption distribution. We prove distribution-free one-shot recovery, a high-probability certificate for the future-ciphertext coverage of a sampled span, and the optimal sampled-span complexity [MATH]. These results yield a generic impossibility theorem: publicly samplable linear key transport with polynomial sampled-orbit dimension is incompatible with IND--CPA security when the transported value determines the decryption payload. We apply the framework to the 2024 probabilistic PKE from twisted--skew group rings. Its underlying Computational Twisted--Skew Problem admits a sampler-only linear attack using independently generated public protocol samples, yielding plaintext recovery and constant IND--CPA advantage. Experiments verify the linear transport and end-to-end recovery, and show that high future-ciphertext coverage may precede recovery of the full algebraic span.
tldr: A distribution-free linear-decomposition attack breaks public-key encryption without recovering the secret algebraic action, demonstrating a generic impossibility theorem and applying it to a specific PKE.
motivation: To attack public-key schemes without recovering the secret algebraic action, using only public sampling-and-evaluation oracles, and to show a generic impossibility of IND-CPA security for publicly samplable linear key transport.
method: They model public paired samples under a fixed secret linear transport, define sampled-orbit dimension, prove distribution-free one-shot recovery, high-probability certificate for future-ciphertext coverage, and optimal sampled-span complexity. Then apply to a specific PKE from twisted--skew group rings.
result: They prove a generic impossibility theorem and demonstrate a sampler-only linear attack on the targeted PKE, achieving plaintext recovery and constant IND-CPA advantage. Experiments confirm the transport and recovery.
conclusion: Publicly samplable linear key transport with polynomial sampled-orbit dimension is incompatible with IND-CPA security, and the attack framework is effective.

title: On The Additive Fft Techniques Over Binary Extension Fields
authors: Susanta Samanta, Mohammadtaghi Badakhshan, Guang Gong
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by Bailey's four-step FFT algorithm (1989), we develop additive FFT techniques for polynomial evaluation over affine subspaces of binary extension fields. Our key insight is that the Taylor expansion with respect to vanishing polynomials of subspaces provides a structural counterpart to Bailey's matrix formulation. It decomposes an additive FFT (AFFT) into independent sub-AFFTs associated with the columns and rows of a matrix. We first present a general-basis AFFT that applies to any ordered basis and any split of the dimension, providing a unified baseline for measuring the gains from specialization. We then specialize the framework to the Cantor special basis and obtain two AFFT algorithms. The first supports an arbitrary decomposition of the AFFT dimension and exploits the Cantor special basis structure to perform the Taylor expansion stage without finite field multiplications. The second uses a decomposition that preserves the binomial form of the relevant subspace polynomials. It requires exactly [MATH] multiplications, together with a closed-form addition count determined by the binary representation of [MATH]. Our implementation results show that this algorithm is faster than the LCH AFFT over a Cantor special basis in 37 of the 42 configurations tested across two hardware platforms. This performance advantage stems from its fully recursive structure, which provides memory locality by design and avoids separate basis-conversion and evaluation stages. Finally, in a separate analysis, we formalize the notion of partial Cantor special bases and identify parameter regimes in which both the von zur Gathen-Gerhard algorithm and our general-basis AFFT require fewer additions and multiplications than the first Gao-Mateer algorithm.
tldr: The paper develops efficient additive FFT algorithms for polynomial evaluation over binary extension fields, improving on existing methods.
motivation: To optimize polynomial evaluation over affine subspaces of binary extension fields, which is fundamental for coding theory and cryptography.
method: Uses Taylor expansion with respect to vanishing polynomials to decompose additive FFTs into independent sub-FFTs, and specializes to the Cantor basis to reduce multiplications.
result: Presents a general-basis AFFT and two specialized algorithms, with one requiring exactly n log n multiplications and outperforming the LCH AFFT in most tested configurations.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a unified baseline and practical algorithms that are faster and more memory-efficient than existing approaches.

title: Extensions Of Courcelle's Theorem Without Logic
authors: Johann A. Makowsky Yuval Filmus
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Courcelle's Theorem states that on graphs [MATH] of tree-width at most [MATH] with a given tree-decomposition of size [MATH], graph properties [MATH] definable in Monadic Second Order Logic can be checked in linear time in the size of [MATH]. Inspired by L. Lov\'asz' work using connection matrices instead of logic, we give a generalized version of Courcelle's theorem which replaces the definability hypothesis by a purely combinatorial hypothesis using a generalization of connection matrices. This paper clarifies the role of logic in such theorems and displays their purely combinatorial assumption.
tldr: This paper generalizes Courcelle's theorem by replacing the logical definability hypothesis with a purely combinatorial condition based on connection matrices.
motivation: To understand and clarify the role of logic in graph property checking, inspired by Lovász's work on connection matrices.
method: The authors replace Monadic Second Order Logic definability with a generalized version of connection matrices, providing a purely combinatorial hypothesis for linear-time checking of graph properties on bounded tree-width.
result: A generalized version of Courcelle's theorem that does not rely on logic, demonstrating that the combinatorial assumption alone suffices.
conclusion: The paper shows that logic is not essential for such theorems, and the combinatorial framework via connection matrices captures the essence.

title: TraceGrant: A Contract-Governed Security Framework For The Task-Effect Lifecycle Of Networked Llm Agents
authors: Bohao Liao, Jingchao Wang, Qipeng Song, Jin Cao, Jieling Wang, Boyu Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Networked large language model (LLM) agents retrieve information from email, cloud storage, calendars, transaction platforms, and Web services to complete multistep tasks that produce persistent external effects. The same content needed for legitimate execution may also contain indirect prompt injections that redirect tool use, alter sensitive arguments, or disrupt task completion. Existing defenses mainly constrain untrusted content or individual tool calls, leaving user intent, runtime evidence, realized effects, and task completion insufficiently connected. We present TraceGrant, a security framework that governs the task-effect lifecycle of networked LLM agents through an explicit Contract. Before execution, TraceGrant establishes a task-effect boundary from the trusted user request. During execution, admitted evidence can instantiate only authority already established by the Contract. After execution, task completion is verified against actual tool results. Across 949 AgentDojo and 400 Agent Security Bench attack cases under fixed benchmark settings, TraceGrant recorded no attack successes while retaining utility under attack rates of 77.32% and 83.00%, respectively. We further evaluate TraceGrant through white-box defense-aware attacks, Contract quality analysis, stage ablations, targeted stress tests, and runtime overhead measurements. The results show that TraceGrant provides a unified governance layer that connects trusted user intent, runtime evidence, concrete tool execution, and verified task completion.
tldr: TraceGrant is a security framework for networked LLM agents that uses a contract-governed approach to prevent indirect prompt injection attacks.
motivation: Existing defenses for LLM agents do not adequately connect user intent, runtime evidence, realized effects, and task completion, leaving security gaps.
method: It establishes a task-effect boundary from trusted user requests, admits only evidence within the contract's authority during execution, and verifies task completion against actual tool results.
result: Across 949 AgentDojo and 400 Agent Security Bench attack cases, TraceGrant recorded no attack successes while retaining utility under attack rates of 77.32% and 83.00%.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified governance layer that connects trusted user intent, runtime evidence, concrete tool execution, and verified task completion.

title: Billion-Scale Nearest-Neighbor Search Under Fully Homomorphic Encryption On A Single Gpu, Balancing Leakage And Cost
authors: Isamu Isozaki, Madison Bratina, Edward Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We build a system that answers "which database vectors are most similar to my query?" without the server ever seeing the query. The query is encrypted with fully homomorphic en- cryption (FHE); the server does all its scoring on ciphertexts and returns encrypted results that only the client can read. The challenge is speed: at a billion vectors, scoring every row under encryption is far too slow, so we combine two ideas - rank reduction (shrink each vector's dimen- sion) and a hierarchy (route to a small candidate set instead of scanning everything) - executed under encryption on a single GPU. We evaluate on three corpora at very different scales: a face corpus of 222 049 centroids clustered from ~10 M face images (512-dim), DataComp-1B (1.39 x 10^9 vectors, 512-dim CLIP), and Deep1B (10^9 vectors, 96-dim). On DataComp-1B we reach a recall@10 of 0.90 against the single labeled answer, or 0.95 when a near-duplicate im- age in the top-10 also counts as correct (the data is web-scraped and full of duplicates), at ~6 s per encrypted query on a GPU; a lighter configuration reaches 0.78/0.83 at ~1.8 s. These are warm (deployable) server-side latencies - client decryption and network transfer are excluded. On Deep1B we reach recall@10 0.90 under all-levels FHE (0.9045 measured over 2000 FHE queries, matching the 0.906 plaintext routing - the 96 -> 128 zero-pad is exact, correlation 1.0) at 2.3 s warm per query. We describe the full client-server protocol in enough detail to repro- duce it, and report accuracy and latency for every configuration. We also measure what this speed costs: the hierarchy's access pattern leaks the database geometry (an observer recovers 72% of the coarse-cell neighbor graph from access patterns alone), and we show that seeded (fixed-group) padding cuts this leak by ~35x (to ~2%), where naive padding is defeated by a repeated-query attack.
tldr: This paper presents a system for private billion-scale nearest-neighbor search using fully homomorphic encryption on a GPU, achieving fast query times while managing privacy leakage.
motivation: To enable clients to search over large databases without revealing their queries to the server, using FHE to encrypt queries.
method: Combines rank reduction and hierarchical routing to reduce the search space, executes all operations under FHE on a single GPU, and analyzes the access-pattern leakage.
result: Achieves recall@10 of 0.90 on DataComp-1B at ~6s per query, and 0.90 on Deep1B at 2.3s, with methods to reduce leakage via seeded padding.
conclusion: Demonstrates practical private nearest-neighbor search at scale, balancing accuracy, speed, and privacy leakage.

title: Abstract Computation Over First-order Structures. Extras: From Programs To Decision Trees I
authors: Christine Ga{\ss}ner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decisions and their consequences can be described and analyzed by means of decision trees. The decisions themselves depend on questions that, whenever possible, should be answered with yes or no. The original BSS machines over the real numbers are graphs with computation nodes and branching nodes for decisions. The evaluation of BSS machines and algebraic decision trees in computer-aided geometry which have been introduced for various types of numbers generally involves the evaluation of systems of literals of first-order logic. Flowchart-like representations and decision trees are also helpful for analyzing decisions made by BSS RAMs over first-order structures. All algorithms defined by machine-oriented programs of BSS RAMs can be illustrated using flowcharts, walks, and paths in program trees. The basic structures of these tools are graphs and their visual representations can help to characterize the behavior of individual BSS RAMs and other first-order machines. We offer a theoretical framework for linking various models. Here, we introduce program paths and transition systems for transforming partial configurations which are defined syntactically and can be extended and refined later. Finally, we define standard orders for program paths and present algorithms for enumerating finite program paths.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for representing BSS RAM programs over first-order structures using decision trees and transition systems, with algorithms for enumerating finite program paths.
motivation: To link various computational models (e.g., BSS machines, algebraic decision trees) and analyze decisions via a unified formal framework.
method: Introduces program paths and transition systems defined syntactically, and presents algorithms for enumerating finite program paths.
result: Provides a formal basis for characterizing the behavior of BSS RAMs and other first-order machines using graphs, flowcharts, and decision trees.
conclusion: Establishes a theoretical foundation for further extensions and refinements, supporting analysis of machine-oriented programs beyond classical models.

title: Faults That Fortify: Cnn Adversarial Robustness Via Gpu Undervolting
authors: Behnam Omidi, Ahmad Tahmasivand, Husam Alsyouri, Saba Al-Sayouri, Chongzhou Fang, Ihsen Alouani, Khaled N. Khasawneh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) face a dual challenge: vulnerability to adversarial attacks and prohibitive training cost. Adversarial training is effective but expensive, a burden that grows as learning shifts to the energy-constrained edge. This paper addresses both through GPU undervolting during training. Reducing supply voltage introduces stochastic perturbations that act as implicit regularization, improving robustness while lowering power. We characterize undervolting-induced faults at the bit level, then train LeNet, VGG-6, and MobileNetV3 on MNIST and CIFAR-10 under two training regimes, standard and adversarial, each at nominal and undervolted voltage, and evaluate all models against adversarial attacks. In both regimes, the undervolted model consistently achieves higher adversarial accuracy than its nominal-voltage counterpart, showing that hardware-induced faults strengthen even adversarial training. Because dynamic power scales quadratically with supply voltage, these robustness gains arrive with substantial energy savings. GPU undervolting is therefore a readily deployable hardware-level defense requiring no algorithmic change, and opens a promising direction in which robustness and energy efficiency move together.
tldr: This paper shows that undervolting GPUs during CNN training introduces bit-level faults that act as regularization, improving adversarial robustness while reducing energy consumption.
motivation: Adversarial training is expensive, and edge devices have energy constraints; the paper explores hardware-induced perturbations as a low-cost robustness enhancer.
method: They characterize undervolting-induced faults at bit level, then train LeNet, VGG-6, MobileNetV3 on MNIST/CIFAR-10 under standard and adversarial training at nominal and undervolted voltages, and evaluate against adversarial attacks.
result: Undervolted models consistently achieve higher adversarial accuracy than nominal-voltage counterparts, with substantial energy savings.
conclusion: GPU undervolting is a deployable hardware-level defense that improves robustness and energy efficiency without algorithmic changes.

title: Cdrl: Certification-Driven Reinforcement Learning For Neutrino Flavor Model Discovery
authors: Piyush Jha, Jake Rudolph, Victoria Knapp-P\'erez, Max Fieg, Aishik Ghosh, Vijay Ganesh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many scientific discovery problems require searching combinatorial hypothesis spaces under complex domain constraints. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising approach, but existing methods rely on scalar rewards that provide limited information about why candidate solutions fail, leading agents to repeatedly explore invalid regions. We introduce Certification-Driven Reinforcement Learning (CDRL), a framework that leverages structured feedback from symbolic reasoning tools. When a candidate violates domain constraints, these tools produce certificates identifying the actions responsible for failure. CDRL converts these certificates into reusable constraints that eliminate classes of invalid solutions and guide exploration toward valid regions. We evaluate CDRL on neutrino flavor model discovery in theoretical particle physics, where the hypothesis space exceeds [MATH] possible models, and compare it with the state-of-the-art RL approach previously used for this task. Across three theory spaces, CDRL achieves up to 1.95[MATH] higher valid model rates and up to 6.33[MATH] higher neutrino model rates while evaluating up to 4[MATH] fewer candidates. We further extract 40 interpretable rules from search trajectories using a post-hoc decision-tree framework and show that reusing them as soft constraints yields gains of up to 2[MATH] in valid model rates and 3[MATH] in neutrino model discovery across all three theory spaces. These results suggest that CDRL uncovers reusable structure in combinatorial search spaces and provides a general framework for scientific model discovery.
tldr: Introduces a reinforcement learning framework that uses certificates from symbolic reasoning to guide exploration in combinatorial hypothesis spaces, applied to neutrino flavor model discovery in particle physics.
motivation: Existing RL methods for scientific discovery rely on scalar rewards that give limited feedback, causing agents to explore invalid regions repeatedly.
method: CDRL converts certificates from symbolic reasoning tools into reusable constraints that prune invalid solutions and guide exploration; evaluated on neutrino flavor model discovery.
result: Achieves up to 1.95x higher valid model rates and 6.33x higher neutrino model rates while evaluating fewer candidates; extracts interpretable rules that further improve performance.
conclusion: CDRL uncovers reusable structure in combinatorial search spaces and provides a general framework for scientific model discovery.

title: Privacy-Preserving Localization Via Transmit Antenna Selection And Permutation
authors: Yiyang Zhang, Yanmo Hu, Junyuan Gao, Shuowen Zhang, Jiannong Cao, Liang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been identified as one primary usage scenario in the sixth-generation (6G) network. While techniques to preserve information privacy, such as cryptography, have been widely investigated, how to preserve sensing privacy is still an open problem in the literature. This paper makes an early attempt to tackle the above issue. Specifically, we consider a localization system consisting of a multi-antenna transmitter, termed Alice, a single-antenna legitimate receiver, termed Bob, and a single-antenna illegitimate receiver, termed Eve. To allow Bob to estimate Alice's angle-of-departure (AOD) but prevent Eve from performing this task based on Alice's signals, this paper proposes a novel antenna selection and permutation based transmission strategy for Alice. Under this scheme, Alice carefully selects a subset of antennas and permutes their indices to establish a specific pilot-antenna mapping for transmission. Similar to cryptography for information privacy, such a mapping will serve as the secret key to preserve localization privacy. In the special case without noise at Bob and Eve, we manage to find out all the antenna selection and permutation solutions such that with this key (knowledge about the exact pilot-antenna mapping), Bob can uniquely estimate Alice's AOD, while without this key, Eve can estimate multiple AODs of Alice that can lead to its received signals. In the noisy case, numerical results are provided to show that our scheme can confuse Eve to make inaccurate AOD estimation as well.
tldr: This paper proposes a transmit antenna selection and permutation strategy for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to enable legitimate receivers to estimate angle-of-departure while preventing eavesdroppers, using a secret antenna-mapping key.
motivation: Preserving sensing privacy in ISAC is an open problem; existing work focuses on information privacy (cryptography), not privacy of sensing parameters like localization.
method: Alice, a multi-antenna transmitter, selects a subset of antennas and permutes their indices to create a secret pilot-antenna mapping. Bob knows the mapping and can uniquely estimate AOD, while Eve without the key cannot.
result: In the noiseless case, all feasible antenna selection and permutation solutions are characterized for which Bob uniquely recovers AOD but Eve cannot. In noisy conditions, numerical results show Eve's AOD estimation accuracy degrades.
conclusion: The proposed scheme effectively confuses eavesdroppers, but in noisy scenarios it only degrades Eve's estimation rather than preventing it entirely, indicating a trade-off between privacy and reliability.

title: The Effective Gravitational Field Of The Ball In Association Football
authors: Oliver B. Wright
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In association football, collective player motion is organized around the ball. We ask whether this many-agent response can be described by an effective field analogous to gravitational attraction, while emphasizing that the measured quantity is a radial drift velocity of the players, as in an overdamped system, rather than a Newtonian acceleration. Using public tracking data from three anonymized games, we form two averages of the same player radial drift values: the distance-dependent radial drift velocity D(r), obtained by averaging at fixed player-ball distance, and the ball-position drift velocity field K(x,y), obtained by averaging the same inward velocity over observations in which the ball lies in a given pitch cell. After excluding restarts, other constrained phases of play, the nearest player to the ball, and separations r < 2 m, a persistent inward drift remains, with a global mean of 0.70 +/- 0.05 m/s. The distance dependence is not well described by inverse powers of r: moving outward from the ball, D(r) falls to a shallow minimum near r approximately 12 m, rises to a positive mid-range plateau, and then decreases toward zero at the largest separations. The full curve is summarized by a compact empirical drift law. The drift field K(x,y) is broadly positive over most of the pitch, but its three-game mean has a shallow central depression, about 25 percent below the non-goalmouth average, and stronger suppression near the central goalmouths, where the mean drift can become slightly negative. Including the player nearest to the ball or excluding goalkeepers leaves the radial law and drift-field pattern essentially unchanged. Football tracking data can therefore be used to extract simple effective laws of active many-body motion.
tldr: This paper analyzes football tracking data to see if player motion around the ball can be described by an effective gravitational field, finding a persistent inward drift velocity but with non-Newtonian behavior.
motivation: The authors aim to understand collective many-agent motion in football, using an analogy to gravity, and to extract simple empirical laws from tracking data.
method: Using public tracking data from three anonymized games, they compute radial drift velocities of players relative to the ball, averaging them by distance and position, while excluding restarts, constrained phases, and the nearest player.
result: A persistent inward drift with a global mean of 0.70 ± 0.05 m/s is observed. The distance dependence shows a characteristic curve with a shallow minimum and mid-range plateau, not fitting inverse power laws. The drift field is broadly positive but suppressed near goalmouths.
conclusion: Football tracking data can be used to extract effective laws of active many-body motion, though the effective gravitational analogy is limited and not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Peer-Voted LLM-Agent Stress Tests Find Feed-Induced Lexical Convergence But No Reliable Matched-Exposure Advantage For Distributed Sources
authors: Dominic Williamson Rana Muhammad Usman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Population-level behavior in large-language-model (LLM) agents cannot be characterized by single-agent benchmarks. We introduce PV-SST, a peer-voted social-platform testbed, and report a separately frozen, preregistered matched-exposure experiment spanning four topics, four unused seeds, four open-weight model families, and three prespecified larger variants. The experiment comprises 448 trials and 112 complete model-by-topic-by-seed blocks. Relative to a topic-only control, a feed of previous-round peer posts ranked by peer-generated likes increases final-round lexical similarity in both the four-family core panel (paired mean difference +0.0082 TF-IDF cosine units, 95% block-bootstrap CI [0.0043, 0.0121], randomization p=0.000105, n=64 blocks) and the three-variant size extension (+0.0109 [0.0069, 0.0151], p=0.000001, n=48). This contrast bundles peer-post exposure with ranking and therefore does not identify a ranking-only effect. Opposite-side survival falls in the core panel (-3.9 percentage points [-6.8, -1.6], p=0.0068) but not conclusively in the larger variants (-1.0 pp [-3.1, 0.4], p=0.50). Holding adversarial impressions fixed, four distributed sources do not reliably move honest-agent stance more than one source. The preregistered distributed-minus-single contrast is positive but inconclusive in the core panel (+0.057 [-0.009, 0.125], p=0.112) and negative in the larger variants (-0.040 [-0.113, 0.035], p=0.332), failing the prespecified cross-model and cross-topic consistency criterion. Thus the robust result is lexical convergence under the tested peer-ranked feed, not general opinion capture or a general coordination advantage. The study evaluates synthetic LLM-agent populations; it does not estimate effects on people or production platforms.
tldr: Investigates whether social feed exposure causes lexical convergence in LLM agent populations, finding feed-induced convergence but no reliable distributed-source advantage.
motivation: Population-level behavior in LLM agents cannot be characterized by single-agent benchmarks; need collective tests.
method: Preregistered matched-exposure experiment with 448 trials across 4 topics, 4 seeds, 4 model families, comparing peer-ranked feed vs topic-only control, measuring lexical similarity.
result: Peer-ranked feed significantly increases lexical similarity (e.g., +0.0082 TF-IDF cosine), but distributed sources do not reliably move stance more than a single source.
conclusion: Robust effect is lexical convergence under peer-ranked feed; no evidence for general opinion capture or coordination advantage.

title: Beat-spectrum Design For 100-km-range Optical Correlation-domain Reflectometry With Localized 15-cm Resolution
authors: Takaki Kiyozumi, Yuta Higa, Soshi Yoshida, Keisuke Motoda, Sze Yun Set, Shinji Yamashita, Yosuke Mizuno
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional optical correlation-domain reflectometry (OCDR) based on sinusoidal frequency modulation exhibits a coupling between measurement range and spatial resolution because both are governed by the modulation frequency. Here, we formulate OCDR for arbitrary periodic frequency modulation and relate the modulation waveform to the resulting beat spectrum. By expressing the instantaneous optical frequency as a Fourier series, the beat spectrum is written as successive convolutions of the spectral contributions from the harmonic components. This formulation relates the harmonic composition of the modulation waveform to the spatial response. Periodic pseudo-random modulation (PPRM) was used to test this relation experimentally. We first measured the full-length reflectivity distribution along an approximately 100-km fiber using sinusoidal modulation and then performed PPRM-based random access interrogation near the fiber end. In the local measurement, two closely spaced reflection points were resolved with a correlation-peak width of approximately 15 cm. These results show that beat-spectrum design can reduce the range-resolution coupling of conventional sinusoidal-modulation OCDR and combine long-range surveying with localized high-resolution interrogation.
tldr: This paper presents a general formulation for optical correlation-domain reflectometry (OCDR) with arbitrary periodic frequency modulation, enabling independent control of measurement range and spatial resolution, and demonstrates 15-cm resolution over a 100-km fiber using periodic pseudo-random modulation.
motivation: Conventional OCDR with sinusoidal modulation couples measurement range and spatial resolution, both governed by the modulation frequency, limiting performance. The authors aim to break this coupling by designing the beat spectrum through arbitrary periodic modulation.
method: They express the instantaneous optical frequency as a Fourier series, deriving the beat spectrum as successive convolutions of harmonic contributions. Experimental validation employs periodic pseudo-random modulation (PPRM) to test the relation between modulation waveform and spatial response.
result: Full-length reflectivity distribution over ~100 km was obtained with sinusoidal modulation, and PPRM-based random access near the fiber end resolved two closely spaced reflections with a correlation-peak width of ~15 cm.
conclusion: Beat-spectrum design effectively reduces range-resolution coupling in OCDR, allowing combination of long-range surveying with localized high-resolution interrogation.

title: Sidewall-Poled Nanophotonic Lithium Niobate With Bidirectional Characterization
authors: Aditya Tripathi, Michael S. Bullock, Parash Thapalia, Pooja Kulkarni, Jaber Balalhabashi, Robert Kwolek, Shiva Behzadfar, Kazuki Hirota, Shion Eto, Rintaro Tsuchida, Liam Beaudoin, Sasan Fathpour, Rajveer Nehra
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate characterization of integrated nonlinear photonic devices is often limited by unknown facet-coupling losses and fabrication-induced non-uniformities, leading to systematic over- or underestimation of the intrinsic on-chip performance. Here, we present and demonstrate a unified bidirectional characterization framework that exploits nonlinear interactions under forward and backward propagation to independently extract facet-specific coupling efficiencies, intrinsic nonlinear conversion efficiency, and the longitudinal quasi-phase-matching profile using only classical power measurements. We experimentally validate the method using sidewall-poled thin-film lithium niobate waveguides, obtaining a normalized second-harmonic generation efficiency of [MATH] while simultaneously demonstrating broadband non-degenerate optical parametric amplification and parametric generation spanning more than [MATH]. Our framework is non-destructive, relies solely on classical power measurements, requires neither time-intensive microscopy nor calibrated internal references, and is compatible with wafer-scale testing, providing a general route to rigorous benchmarking and high-throughput characterization of photonic devices across material platforms.
tldr: This paper presents a bidirectional characterization framework for integrated nonlinear photonic devices, demonstrated on sidewall-poled lithium niobate waveguides, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.
motivation: To accurately characterize on-chip nonlinear photonic devices by separating facet-coupling losses from intrinsic conversion efficiency, addressing limitations of existing methods.
method: Exploits forward and backward propagation of classical power measurements to extract facet coupling efficiencies, intrinsic nonlinear conversion efficiency, and quasi-phase-matching profile without internal references.
result: Achieves normalized SHG efficiency and demonstrates broadband optical parametric amplification/generation, validating the method experimentally.
conclusion: The framework provides a general, non-destructive, wafer-scale-compatible route for benchmarking photonic devices, but is unrelated to the specified research directions.

title: Two-dimensional Percolation With Algebraically Decaying Interactions Ii: Critical Exponents In The Long-range Regime
authors: Ziyu Liu, Tianning Xiao, Zhijie Fan, Youjin Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive Monte Carlo study of two-dimensional bond percolation with algebraically decaying connection probabilities [MATH], establishing the universality diagram in the long-range (LR) regime for [MATH]. Using the event-based ensemble method, we simulate systems with linear sizes up to [MATH] and investigate three universality regimes: LR Wilson--Fisher (WF) A ([MATH]), LR Wilson--Fisher B ([MATH]), and LR mean-field (MF) ([MATH]). In the LR-WF-B regime, the anomalous dimension is consistent with [MATH], in agreement with mathematical results for [MATH], while the correlation-length exponent [MATH] exhibits nontrivial, non-Gaussian variation. In the LR-WF-A regime, although [MATH] remains close to [MATH] for smaller [MATH], statistically resolvable deviations [MATH] start to appear near [MATH] and grow toward the short-range crossover at [MATH]. Finally, by complementing the event-based simulations with conventional ensemble simulations, we reveal the coexistence of complete-graph asymptotics and LR Gaussian-fixed-point scaling in the LR-MF regime. These results further clarify the critical properties in long-range percolation and provide crucial benchmarks for long-range statistical systems.
tldr: A Monte Carlo study of critical exponents in two-dimensional bond percolation with long-range interactions.
motivation: To clarify critical properties and universality in long-range percolation systems.
method: Event-based ensemble and conventional Monte Carlo simulations with large system sizes.
result: Identified three universality regimes and observed nontrivial variations in critical exponents.
conclusion: Provides benchmarks for long-range statistical systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Direction-Selective Wave Freezing And Amplification At A Hyperbolic Time Interface
authors: Zhao Wang, Ai Gang, Xinghong Zhu, Hongru Ma, Wen Xiao, Huanyang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperbolic media are well known for converting high k-components that are evanescent in conventional dielectrics into propagating bulk waves through their open equifrequency contours. Here, we reveal a complementary temporal effect: after a sudden transition into an effectively nondispersive hyperbolic state, conservation of the full wavevector causes the indefinite dispersion to partition momentum space into real-, zero-, and purely imaginary-frequency regimes. Consequently, p-polarized waves undergo conventional temporal scattering, critical magnetic-field freezing, or exponential growth and decay, depending solely on their conserved wavevector direction, whereas s-polarized waves remain in the real-frequency regime. A second temporal boundary releases the frozen or amplified fields into propagating waves at original frequency. Analytical temporal boundary theory, k-space pulse reconstruction, and finite-difference time-domain simulations corroborate these dynamics. These results establish hyperbolic temporal boundaries as a compact route to direction-selective imaginary frequency dynamics and wave amplification without Floquet periodicity.
tldr: This paper explores wave dynamics at a temporal interface into a hyperbolic state, demonstrating direction-selective wave freezing and amplification based on wavevector direction.
motivation: To investigate temporal effects in hyperbolic media, complementing known spatial effects, and to achieve wave amplification without periodic driving.
method: Analytical temporal boundary theory, k-space pulse reconstruction, and finite-difference time-domain simulations.
result: P-polarized waves exhibit conventional scattering, freezing, or exponential growth/decay depending on wavevector direction, while s-polarized waves remain real; a second boundary releases frozen/amplified fields.
conclusion: Hyperbolic temporal boundaries offer a compact route to direction-selective imaginary frequency dynamics and wave amplification, without relying on Floquet periodicity.

title: Total Inner Products And Cyclic Chern-Simons Forms
authors: Jake P. Solomon Pavel Giterman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of a total inner product on an [MATH]-algebra, and a cyclic Chern-Simons form associated to a topologically nilpotent element. The total inner product applied to the cyclic Chern-Simons form gives a superpotential function that is gauge invariant on solutions of the Maurer-Cartan equation known as bounding cochains. The derivative of the superpotential is computed. The definition of total inner product replaces strict symmetries that appear in previous notions of homotopy inner products with symmetries up to an infinite family of coherent homotopies. We show how to recover previous notions of homotopy inner products as special cases of total inner products. Total inner products are designed to facilitate the definition of descendent open Gromov-Witten invariants. The definitions of the total inner product and the cyclic Chern-Simons form use the total complex of cyclic codifferential forms, which gives a chain model for cyclic homology. We give explicit formulas for homotopy equivalences with other known models. We discuss also the notion of an [MATH]-trace, which arises from Connes' cyclic complex, and the associated [MATH]-modulus, which gives another gauge-invariant function on bounding cochains. In open Gromov-Witten theory, the [MATH]-modulus is used to normalize the bounding cochains to which the superpotential is applied. We develop our definitions for general curved Banach [MATH]-algebras, and give both unital and non-unital versions of the main results. In the unital setting, we work with weak bounding cochains, solutions of an inhomogeneous Maurer-Cartan equation involving the unit. Weak bounding cochains arise in the open Gromov-Witten theory of Lagrangian submanifolds with non-vanishing Maslov class. The derivative of the superpotential at a weak bounding cochain is related to the derivative of the [MATH]-modulus.
tldr: The paper introduces total inner products and cyclic Chern-Simons forms for A∞-algebras to define gauge-invariant superpotentials on bounding cochains, with applications to open Gromov-Witten invariants.
motivation: The paper aims to develop mathematical tools for defining descendent open Gromov-Witten invariants, generalizing homotopy inner products with coherent symmetries.
method: It uses the total complex of cyclic codifferential forms to construct a chain model for cyclic homology, and provides explicit formulas for homotopy equivalences with other models.
result: It defines total inner products and cyclic Chern-Simons forms, showing they generalize previous homotopy inner products, and computes derivatives of superpotentials for weak bounding cochains.
conclusion: The work is purely mathematical, focusing on algebraic structures in symplectic topology, with no direct relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A New Analysis Of The Randomly Pivoted Cholesky Algorithm
authors: Ethan N. W. Epperly
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The randomly pivoted Cholesky algorithm is one of the leading methods for computing a low-rank approximation to a large positive-semidefinite matrix. However, while it consistently achieves accuracy comparable to or better than competing methods of its type in experiments, its theoretical analysis lags somewhat behind other methods. This paper closes this gap, proving that randomly pivoted Cholesky produces an approximation with expected error within a [MATH] factor of the optimal rank-[MATH] approximation in [MATH] steps. This result nearly matches the optimal complexity [MATH] for any low-rank approximation method based on a partial Cholesky decomposition (also known as a column Nystr\"om approximation). The paper also presents bounds on the randomly pivoted Cholesky trace and spectral-norm errors that hold with high probability. The mathematical argument is largely due to GPT 5.6-Sol (Pro), with some refinements by the author.
tldr: This paper provides a new theoretical analysis of the randomly pivoted Cholesky algorithm, proving near-optimal error bounds for low-rank approximation of positive-semidefinite matrices.
motivation: The algorithm is widely used but lacks rigorous theoretical guarantees, lagging behind other methods in analysis.
method: The work employs mathematical proof techniques, likely including probabilistic analysis, to establish expected error bounds and high-probability spectral and trace norm bounds.
result: It shows that the algorithm achieves an approximation error within a constant factor of the optimal rank-k approximation in O(k) steps, nearly matching the optimal complexity.
conclusion: The analysis resolves the gap between empirical performance and theoretical understanding, confirming the algorithm's effectiveness.

title: Strong Growth And Goldstein Subgradients In Piecewise Smooth Optimization
authors: Fahaar M. Pirani Adrian S. Lewis
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore a new growth condition for Lipschitz functions around local minimizers, recently proposed in the context of Goldstein-subgradient-based algorithms and their behavior in practice. On generic examples, these algorithms are often observed to converge approximately linearly. We focus on objectives that are piecewise twice continuously differentiable. In that case, the new growth condition holds when the objective is, in addition, strongly convex. In the nonconvex case, we prove that quadratic growth in conjunction with a regularity property for the active gradients suffices. Computational experiments illustrate the importance of the assumptions.
tldr: Introduces a new growth condition for Lipschitz functions and proves it holds for piecewise smooth objectives under convexity or quadratic growth assumptions, explaining convergence of Goldstein-subgradient algorithms.
motivation: To understand why Goldstein-subgradient-based algorithms often exhibit approximate linear convergence on generic examples.
method: Analyzes piecewise twice continuously differentiable objectives, proving the growth condition holds under strong convexity or quadratic growth with a regularity property on active gradients.
result: Provides theoretical guarantees for the growth condition and demonstrates the importance of assumptions via computational experiments.
conclusion: The growth condition is validated for a class of nonconvex piecewise smooth functions, matching observed algorithm behavior.

title: ResiliFlow: An Open Transport World Model For Infrastructure Perception And Disaster Resilience
authors: Junxiang Xu (vivian), Vinayak Dixit (vivian), S. Travis Waller (vivian), Divya Jayakumar Nair (vivian), Qianwen (vivian), Guo, Sisi Jian, Xiao Wen, Ashutosh Ashutosh, Sunhyung Yoo, Julius Secadiningrat, Jingni Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transport resilience work is often split across separate data preparation scripts, network models, simulation tools, image inspection systems and reports. This fragmentation makes it difficult to move from an observation to a tested and reviewable decision. We introduce ResiliFlow, an open transport world model concept and an implemented platform for infrastructure resilience, response and recovery. The platform connects two workspaces. Disaster Transport Resilience Analysis provides six map-centred functions for critical-road and critical-area identification, recovery prioritisation, disruption routing, resilience testing and scenario simulation. AI-based Transport Infrastructure Perception and Decision Support organises street-level and satellite evidence, detects visible road, footpath and kerb conditions, and prepares these observations for human-reviewed intervention planning. Both workspaces share an eight-step cycle of perception, prediction, model development, verification, execution, decision, feedback and memory. Research Validation records assumptions and checks, while a local Assistant and an optional multi-provider large language model Copilot translate user questions into bounded calls to executable tools. We document the platform architecture, representative mathematical models, interface evidence and computer-vision learning results. Examples show accurate recognition across eight visible-condition classes, while compact error analysis demonstrates how difficult cases guide continued learning. ResiliFlow shows how transport models can become an inspectable, reusable and question-led system rather than a collection of disconnected analyses. The accompanying release is intended to support research collaboration, public scrutiny and extension under institutional review.
tldr: ResiliFlow is an open platform integrating disaster transport resilience analysis with AI-based infrastructure perception to support decision-making and recovery planning.
motivation: Transport resilience work is fragmented across tools, hindering transition from observations to tested decisions. The authors aim to create an integrated, inspectable, and question-led system.
