As an application, we extend the Riemann integral on Dedekind complete [MATH]-algebras to Type I and Type II improper integrals. We conclude by showing that power series on universally complete vector lattices may be integrated term-by-term.
tldr: Introduces a sup-inf-completion for Dedekind complete vector lattices, extending integration theory to improper integrals and power series.
motivation: To provide a canonical order completion that ensures every nonempty subset has both a supremum and an infimum, using the framework of lattice stars.
method: Develops lattice stars and constructs the sup-inf-completion, proving key properties such as universality and representation, and characterizing bands and band projections.
result: Extends the Riemann integral on Dedekind complete f-algebras to Type I and Type II improper integrals, and shows power series on universally complete vector lattices can be integrated term-by-term.
conclusion: The sup-inf-completion offers a novel order-theoretic tool with applications to integration theory, though it has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Counterexample To The Symmetric-maximizer Conjecture For Lyapunov Operators
authors: Bart Vandereycken Daniel Kressner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has been conjectured that the operator norm of the Lyapunov operator induced by the Frobenius norm is always attained at a symmetric matrix. The conjecture is known to hold for all matrices of order at most five. We give an integer matrix of order seven for which the skew-symmetric restricted norm is strictly larger than the symmetric restricted norm. A rational separator and exact-arithmetic certificates establish the strict inequality without relying on floating-point computations. A direct-sum construction yields counterexamples in every order [MATH]; the case [MATH] remains open.
tldr: This paper disproves the symmetric-maximizer conjecture for Lyapunov operators by providing an explicit counterexample for matrices of order 7.
motivation: The conjecture that the operator norm of the Lyapunov operator (induced by the Frobenius norm) is always attained at a symmetric matrix was open; the paper aims to settle it.
method: The authors construct an integer matrix of order 7 and use a rational separator and exact-arithmetic certificates to prove that the skew-symmetric restricted norm exceeds the symmetric restricted norm, avoiding floating-point errors.
result: The counterexample shows the conjecture is false, and a direct-sum construction generalizes it to all orders except possibly one.
conclusion: The symmetric-maximizer conjecture for Lyapunov operators is disproved, but the case where it might hold remains open.

title: Fluid-Antenna-Assisted Distributed Joint Decoding For Cell-Free Massive Mimo Unsourced Random Access
authors: Liandong Hu, Jian Dang, Zaichen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unsourced random access (URA) supports massive sporadic connectivity but remains limited by multiuser interference, distributed channel uncertainty, and local fading. This paper proposes a fluid-antenna-assisted distributed joint decoder for cell-free massive MIMO URA. Single-radio-frequencychain access points sequentially sound correlated ports; the central processor then performs correlation-aware expectationmaximization approximate message passing, selects one common payload port per access point, and combines MIMO iterative Gaussian approximation with full-packet channel re-estimation and successive interference cancellation. Fixed-port ablations confirm the complementary benefits of distributed reception, reestimation, and iterative cancellation, while fluid-antenna simulations show improved average and lower-tail received power over fixed-port reception. The framework provides a feasible integration of fluid antennas and cell-free URA and motivates end-to-end evaluation under pilot collisions and switching overhead.
tldr: This paper proposes a fluid-antenna-assisted distributed joint decoding scheme for cell-free massive MIMO unsourced random access, demonstrating improved performance through fixed-port ablations and fluid-antenna simulations.
motivation: Unsourced random access faces challenges like multiuser interference and distributed channel uncertainty; the paper aims to address these with fluid antennas and distributed joint decoding.
method: The method involves single-RF-chain access points sounding correlated ports, a central processor using correlation-aware expectation maximization approximate message passing, and combining MIMO iterative Gaussian approximation with full-packet channel re-estimation and successive interference cancellation.
result: Fixed-port ablations confirm benefits of distributed reception, reestimation, and iterative cancellation; fluid-antenna simulations show improved average and lower-tail received power.
conclusion: The framework provides feasible integration of fluid antennas and cell-free URA, motivating end-to-end evaluation under pilot collisions and switching overhead.

title: A Harmonic Framework For Vector Fields And Differential Operators On So(3)
authors: Erik W\"unsche Ralf Hielscher
abstract: ArXiv:2608.21235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive framework for tangent vector fields and differential operators on the rotation group [MATH] using harmonic series expansions, which provides a mathematical foundation for their implementation in the crystallographic texture analysis software MTEX. The central idea is to employ the standard left- and right-invariant frames as global orthonormal frames of the tangent bundle, thereby avoiding the numerical instabilities of the classical tangent space basis derived from the Jacobian of the Euler angle parametrization. While the choice of frames is primarily motivated by their geometric and numerical properties, their full potential emerges in the harmonic setting. Representing tangent vector fields through harmonic expansions of their frame components, we derive explicit frequency domain formulas for the gradient, divergence, and curl, allowing these operators to be applied directly to the harmonic coefficients. Moreover, we show that these differential operators preserve harmonic band-limitedness. In addition, the left- and right-invariant representations of tangent vector fields can be transformed into one another directly in the frequency domain, with an increase in harmonic bandwidth of at most one degree.
tldr: This paper presents a harmonic framework for tangent vector fields and differential operators on the rotation group SO(3), aimed at improving numerical stability in crystallographic texture analysis software MTEX.
motivation: The classical tangent space basis derived from Euler angle parametrization suffers from numerical instabilities, motivating the use of global orthonormal frames.
method: The authors employ left- and right-invariant frames as global orthonormal frames, represent vector fields via harmonic expansions, and derive explicit frequency domain formulas for gradient, divergence, and curl.
result: The differential operators preserve harmonic band-limitedness, and transformations between left- and right-invariant representations can be performed directly in the frequency domain with at most one degree increase in harmonic bandwidth.
conclusion: The framework provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for efficient and stable implementation of differential operators on SO(3) in crystallographic texture analysis, with potential applications beyond this field.

title: Aegis: Preventing Cross-Domain Resource Abuse In Mcp
authors: Shriti Priya, Teryl Taylor, Frederico Araujo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open source JSON-RPC protocol that standardizes how large language models (LLMs) interact with external systems through programmatic functions known as tools. Attackers or malicious agents can exploit certain modalities of these MCP tools to degrade the overall quality of service of agent-based applications. For example, an agent may request an excessively large search radius or very long videos, overloading backend systems and potentially causing slowdowns or denial-of-service. Each modality including text, images, video, and location introduces distinct vectors for resource abuse, complicating the development of consistent mitigation strategies. Moreover, multimodal and crossdomain tools expose diverse request schemas and parameters, making it difficult to define policies that are both generalizable and precise enough to enforce meaningful resource constraints. In this paper, we present AEGIS, a policy enforcement component that enables administrators to define fine-grained safeguards against resource abuse across heterogeneous MCP tools and modalities. AEGIS leverages the reasoning capabilities of large language models to analyze, categorize, and normalize diverse tool invocations into a unified, policy-friendly representation accessible to security practitioners. Integrated with the Open Policy Agent and the ContextForge AI Gateway, AEGIS detects and mitigates abusive behaviors while preserving the flexibility of MCP-based agent ecosystems.
tldr: AEGIS is a policy enforcement system that uses LLMs to prevent cross-domain resource abuse in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) by standardizing tool invocations and enforcing fine-grained policies.
motivation: MCP tools are vulnerable to resource abuse via excessive requests, leading to denial-of-service, and existing mitigation strategies are inconsistent across heterogeneous tool modalities and schemas.
method: AEGIS leverages LLMs to analyze, categorize, and normalize diverse tool invocations into a unified representation, and integrates with Open Policy Agent and ContextForge AI Gateway to detect and mitigate abusive behaviors.
result: The system detects and mitigates abusive behaviors while preserving the flexibility of MCP-based agent ecosystems, though specific performance metrics are not provided in the abstract.
conclusion: AEGIS offers a generalizable and precise policy enforcement mechanism to safeguard against resource abuse in LLM-agent tool use.

title: aiXamine: Unified Black-Box Evaluation Of Cross-Dimensional Trade-offs In Llm Safety, Security, And Privacy
authors: Fatih Deniz, Yazan Boshmaf, Dorde Popovic, Issa Khalil
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The critical failure modes in deployed large language models (LLMs) are cross-dimensional: a model can score 99.3 in safety alignment while refusing one in three benign queries, or improve across every capability metric while losing 21 points in privacy. Existing evaluation frameworks that assess safety, security, and privacy independently cannot detect these patterns. We introduce aiXamine, a unified black-box platform that evaluates LLM trustworthiness across safety, security, and privacy as interdependent properties. aiXamine orchestrates 46 tests across nine services through an automated red-teaming pipeline, producing hierarchical risk profiles, from prompt-level diagnostics to cross-service trade-off analytics, that enable reproducible comparison of proprietary and open-weight systems under identical conditions. Applying aiXamine to over 120 LLMs through more than 5,000 test runs, we conduct the largest joint safety, security, and privacy study to date and uncover three cross-dimensional phenomena invisible to single-axis evaluation. First, safety enforcement incurs a quantifiable safety tax: stronger alignment systematically increases over-refusal, forcing providers to choose between protection and utility. Second, privacy is near-orthogonal to other trustworthiness dimensions and not captured by standard alignment. Third, we identify and formally characterize distillation-induced robustness collapse: off-policy distillation without on-policy correction causes entropy collapse, catastrophically destroying robustness (56.9[MATH]2.6) on the same base architecture. These findings, compounded by diminishing returns from scale and category-dependent safety behaviors, demonstrate that trustworthiness is inherently multi-dimensional: progress along one axis does not guarantee, and can actively undermine, progress along others, yet current alignment methods treat it as a single objective.
tldr: Introduces aiXamine, a unified black-box platform for evaluating LLM safety, security, and privacy as interdependent properties, revealing cross-dimensional trade-offs and robustness collapse.
motivation: Existing evaluation frameworks assess safety, security, and privacy independently, missing cross-dimensional failure modes; motivated by the need to detect interconnected trustworthiness issues in LLMs.
method: aiXamine orchestrates 46 tests across nine services via automated red-teaming, producing hierarchical risk profiles and trade-off analytics; applied to over 120 LLMs with 5,000+ test runs.
result: Uncovers safety tax (over-refusal), privacy orthogonality, and distillation-induced robustness collapse; trustworthiness is multi-dimensional.
conclusion: LLM trustworthiness requires joint evaluation across dimensions; progress in one area can undermine others.

title: Beyond End-to-End Success: Diagnosing Failures In Long-Horizon Security Llm Agents
authors: Wei Shao, Chongzhou Fang, Zuxiong Tan, Zequan Liang, Setareh Rafatirad, Avesta Sasan, Houman Homayoun
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon security LLM agents must carry information and decisions across many dependent interactions, where later actions often depend on services, state, or access discovered much earlier. This makes final task success difficult to interpret: an agent may fail before it ever reaches the point where the capability of interest can be exercised. We present a diagnostic methodology that instruments security tasks with checkpoints, separates failures before and after capability exposure, and uses controlled interventions to test suspected upstream bottlenecks. We evaluate the methodology across four task families involving delayed reuse of discovered information, reuse of observed state, recovery from failed strategies, and decision making after uncertain outcomes. On observed state reuse, checkpoint analysis shows that many Gemini 2.5 Flash failures occur before the model observes the state it is later expected to reuse. In a pre-specified 92-seed study, targeted protocol-disambiguation guidance increases state observation from 65.5\% under a matched non-guidance control message to 95.4\%. Repeating the same design with Gemini 3.7 Flash produces the opposite effect, while state observation no longer reliably predicts task completion. These results show that the dominant source of failure can shift across model generations, motivating evaluation that diagnoses where and why long-horizon security agents fail rather than relying only on aggregate task success.
tldr: This paper introduces a diagnostic methodology using checkpoints and controlled interventions to identify where and why long-horizon security LLM agents fail, demonstrating that failure sources can shift across model generations.
motivation: End-to-end success metrics in long-horizon security tasks obscure where failures occur, making it difficult to improve agent performance.
method: The methodology instruments security tasks with checkpoints, separates failures before and after capability exposure, and uses controlled interventions to test bottlenecks across four task families.
result: Checkpoint analysis revealed many failures occur before state observation; protocol-disambiguation guidance significantly improved one model's state observation but had the opposite effect on another, indicating shifting failure sources.
conclusion: Evaluation should focus on diagnosing where and why agents fail rather than relying solely on aggregate task success.

title: Arq: Agentic CodeQL Query Refinement For C/c++ Vulnerability Detection
authors: Chunyi Wang, Yunfei Ke, Junfeng Yang, Yun-Yun Tsai, Penghui Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static analyzers have been widely adopted for vulnerability detection in C/C++ programs. Query-based static analyzers (e.g., CodeQL) encode vulnerable code patterns in detection queries and match them against source code. However, existing queries still suffer from false positives (FPs, incorrectly flagging benign code as vulnerable) and false negatives (FNs, missing real vulnerabilities). We present ARQ, an agentic framework that automatically refines C/C++ CodeQL queries using execution-grounded evidence from synthesized C/C++ programs. Our key insight is that a synthesized program exposes a query's weakness whenever its execution disagrees with the query's verdict. If the program is genuinely vulnerable but the query stays silent, the query has an FN weakness; if the program is safe but the query fires anyway, it has an FP weakness. ARQ then runs an LLM-based refinement loop that repairs the query using these disagreements as ground truth. Unlike previous query refining methods, ARQ requires no labeled datasets, no commit history, and no vulnerability-specific templates. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ARQ by refining 12 official CodeQL queries using three commercial LLMs (GPT-5.4, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, and Gemini-3.5-flash). We compare both ARQ-refined and original CodeQL queries on the Juliet v1.3 and FormAI v2 datasets and show that ARQ-refined queries detect substantially more true positives, by up to 119.8\%, with a Precision of at least 98.0\% throughout. ARQ successfully fixed three unresolved GitHub issues raised in the official CodeQL query repository that had remained open for as long as . The refined queries also exposed two previously undiscovered bugs in the real-world libraries libpng and zlib.
tldr: ARQ is an agentic framework that automatically refines CodeQL queries for C/C++ vulnerability detection using execution-grounded evidence from synthesized programs.
motivation: Existing CodeQL queries suffer from false positives and false negatives, and manual refinement is labor-intensive, requiring labeled data, commit history, or vulnerability-specific templates.
method: ARQ synthesizes C/C++ programs that expose query weaknesses through execution disagreement with the query's verdict, then uses an LLM-based refinement loop to repair the queries using these disagreements as ground truth.
result: Refining 12 official CodeQL queries with three commercial LLMs increased true positives by up to 119.8% with precision at least 98.0%, fixed three unresolved GitHub issues, and uncovered two bugs in libpng and zlib.
conclusion: ARQ demonstrates that agentic query refinement without labeled data or templates can substantially improve the effectiveness of static analysis tools like CodeQL.

title: Privacy-Preserving Object Detection For Vision Transformer-Based Models
authors: Homare Sueyoshi, Kiyoshi Nishikawa, Hitoshi Kiya
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel object detection method that enables us to protect sensitive visual information of test images. Previous studies considering visual information protection focus on image classification tasks. This paper proposes an object detection method using perceptual encryption for the first time. The proposed method can achieve almost the same accuracy as that of models without any protection by utilizing the embedding structure of the Vision Transformer (ViT) and a domain adaptation technique with keys. In experiments, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified in terms of accuracy and visual protection under the use of ViTdet, which is a ViT-based object detection model.
tldr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving object detection method using perceptual encryption and domain adaptation for Vision Transformer models.
motivation: Existing visual information protection methods focus on image classification; this work extends to object detection to protect sensitive visual information in test images.
method: The method integrates perceptual encryption into object detection by leveraging the embedding structure of Vision Transformer (ViT) and a domain adaptation technique with keys.
result: The proposed method achieves nearly the same accuracy as unencrypted models while providing visual protection, as demonstrated with ViTdet.
conclusion: It shows that perceptual encryption can be effectively applied to object detection with ViT-based models, maintaining accuracy with privacy protection.

title: Certified Learning And Equilibrium Implementation Under Opaque Partial Commitment
authors: Xiangtian Li Shuyang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As an extension of existing Bayesian persuasion framework with inadequate message mechanism, we study direct recommendation when a sender is bound by an installed information policy only with probability [MATH], the realization of binding is hidden, and the receiver does not observe the persistent structural environment. The receiver first sees a payoff-neutral, nonmanipulable calibration sample and then faces a fresh, non-certified deployment interaction. In common, the calibration law identifies only the receiver-facing reduced form, not the latent binding and discretionary kernels. We characterize type-wise [MATH]-implementability, construct the receiver's posterior over the full deployment node, and prove a static direct-following implementation theorem. After every calibration history that passes a posterior-predictive obedience test, the deployment assessment is an exact perfect Bayesian equilibrium: Bayes consistency, receiver sequential rationality, sender sequential rationality, and off-path completion are all verified. Under finite-type separation, common recommendation support, and a positive obedience margin, the test activates such an equilibrium with high probability. Our results keep statistical failure probability distinct from equilibrium approximation. Finally, we embed the original robust value frontier, support-wise linear-programming algorithm, and binary-action fractional-knapsack specialization into this implementation framework.
tldr: This paper extends Bayesian persuasion to settings with opaque partial commitment and provides an implementation theorem for perfect Bayesian equilibrium.
motivation: To study direct recommendation when a sender is bound by an installed information policy only with probability, with hidden binding realization and unobserved persistent structural environment.
method: Characterizes type-wise implementability, constructs the receiver's posterior over the full deployment node, and proves a static direct-following implementation theorem.
result: The deployment assessment is an exact perfect Bayesian equilibrium after calibration histories pass a posterior-predictive obedience test, with high probability under finite-type separation.
conclusion: The framework embeds a robust value frontier and linear-programming algorithm, keeping statistical failure probability distinct from equilibrium approximation.

title: Scalpel3: A High-Performance Data Carving Architecture For Recovery Of Fragmented Files
authors: Karley Waguespack, Samuel Goodwin, George Hendrick, Samuel Hildebrand, Thomas Landaiche III, Mingyang Li, Joshua Mccain, Tyler Saizan, Jacob Tucker, James M. Ghawaly, Golden G. Richard III
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: File carving recovers files from raw storage media without relying on filesystem metadata, a key capability in digital forensics, data recovery, and digital exploration. Traditional tools such as Foremost, Scalpel v1/2, and PhotoRec handle contiguous files effectively, and some support fragmented recovery for specific formats under simplifying assumptions, but no publicly available tool provides a general-purpose, high-performance framework for developing and deploying fragmented recovery strategies across many file types at scale. This paper presents Scalpel3, the first general-purpose, open source, massively parallel file carving framework designed to support both contiguous and fragmented recovery at scale. Its primary contribution is an extensible, high-performance architecture that enables researchers to develop, test, and deploy new carving strategies without implementing their own multithreaded backends or I/O infrastructure. Adding support for new file types typically requires only development of single-threaded file validation logic and, where useful, block validation or custom reassembly logic -- the Scalpel3 backend manages parallelization, synchronization, and fast I/O automatically. The architecture also integrates the ONNX Runtime, allowing learned classifiers to participate in block validation and reassembly when useful. Beyond raw performance, Scalpel3 introduces practical features for real-world investigations: persistent checkpointing for long-running jobs, human-in-the-loop control allowing operators to monitor progress and redirect effort interactively, and block-level deduplication to shrink the search space. By making this framework publicly available, we aim to lower barriers to experimentation and help translate file carving research into practitioner-ready tools.
tldr: This paper presents Scalpel3, a general-purpose, parallel file carving framework for recovering fragmented files, targeting digital forensics and data recovery.
motivation: Traditional file carving tools lack general-purpose, high-performance support for fragmented recovery, limiting research and practical deployment.
method: Scalpel3 provides an extensible architecture with multithreaded backends, fast I/O, ONNX Runtime integration for learned classifiers, checkpointing, human-in-the-loop control, and block-level deduplication.
result: The framework enables developing and deploying fragmented recovery strategies across many file types at scale, requiring only single-threaded validation logic from researchers.
conclusion: The authors aim to lower barriers to experimentation and translate file carving research into practitioner-ready tools, making the framework publicly available.

title: Logic-VLA: A Temporal Logic Conditioned Vision-Language-Action Model
authors: Celina Shiyu Wang, Yiqi Zhao, Junjie Ye, Yue Wang, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20556v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models can follow natural-language (NL) task instructions, but such instructions may not precisely specify safety-critical or spatiotemporal requirements on the resulting behavior. We introduce Logic-VLA, a formal-requirement-aware VLA that conditions on Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications supplied at inference time. Logic-VLA uses a syntax-graph-based STL encoder pre-trained to capture temporal logic semantics. Policy adaptation proceeds in two stages: STL-conditioned supervised fine-tuning on satisfying demonstrations is followed by trajectory-level preference optimization over matched satisfying-violating rollout pairs using a flow-matching surrogate for Identity Preference Optimization. This formulation improves formal requirement satisfaction while preserving the nominal NL task. We evaluate Logic-VLA in closed-loop quadcopter navigation simulation across randomized photorealistic environments and test generalization to STL formulas unseen during training. Across the evaluation benchmarks, Logic-VLA improves STL satisfaction rate over an STL-blind base policy by 24.8 to 40.7 percentage points (pp) while reducing nominal NL task success by at most 1.8 pp, showing that a single VLA can adapt its behavior to varying formal requirements without requiring a separate policy for each specification.
tldr: Logic-VLA conditions a vision-language-action model on Signal Temporal Logic specifications to improve formal requirement satisfaction in quadcopter navigation.
motivation: Natural language instructions may not precisely specify safety-critical or spatiotemporal requirements; Logic-VLA aims to incorporate formal specifications.
method: It uses a syntax-graph-based STL encoder and a two-stage training: STL-conditioned supervised fine-tuning followed by trajectory-level preference optimization with a flow-matching surrogate.
result: Logic-VLA improves STL satisfaction rate by 24.8 to 40.7 percentage points over an STL-blind baseline while reducing nominal task success by at most 1.8 pp.
conclusion: A single VLA can adapt to varying formal requirements without needing separate policies per specification.
